am-os-early.title: OpenStax, World History Volume 1, section 3.1: Early Civilizations
am-os-early.notes: Comparative farming and urban development across regional traditions. Textbook synthesis; case studies vary in strength.

am-met-writing.title: Ira Spar, The Origins of Writing (Metropolitan Museum of Art)
am-met-writing.notes: Urban growth, proto-cuneiform and Mesopotamian administrative archives. Institutional texts underrepresent everyday lives.

am-os-mesopotamia.title: OpenStax, World History Volume 1, section 3.2: Ancient Mesopotamia
am-os-mesopotamia.notes: Sumerian city-states, religious institutions, labor, Akkad and Babylon. Secondary overview.

am-met-akkad.title: The Akkadian Period, ca. 2350–2150 BCE (Metropolitan Museum of Art)
am-met-akkad.notes: Early Dynastic political division, Sargon and Akkadian imperial art. Royal chronology and expansion require cross-source interpretation.

am-louvre-vultures.title: Louvre Collections, Stele of the Vultures (Eannatum of Lagash)
am-louvre-vultures.notes: Material, findspot, inscriptions and visual program of royal victory monument. Royal representation is partisan.

am-louvre-hammurabi.title: Musée du Louvre, The Code of Hammurabi
am-louvre-hammurabi.notes: Babylonian law monument, judicial pronouncements and royal legitimation. Not a comprehensive modern statute book or proof of enforcement.

am-met-oldbabylon.title: Elizabeth Knott, The Isin-Larsa and Old Babylonian Periods (Metropolitan Museum of Art)
am-met-oldbabylon.notes: Early second-millennium political transitions, cultural and religious life. Museum synthesis with selective artistic evidence.

am-met-oldassyrian.title: Nancy Highcock, The Old Assyrian Period (Metropolitan Museum of Art)
am-met-oldassyrian.notes: Merchant archives and transregional trade, circa 2000–1600 BCE. Surviving trader letters are not a population survey.

am-os-neareast.title: OpenStax, World History Volume 1, section 4.1: From Old Babylon to the Medes
am-os-neareast.notes: Hammurabi, Hittites, Assyria, diplomacy and social stratification. Textbook overview; distinguish formal rule from social practice.

am-os-egypt.title: OpenStax, World History Volume 1, section 3.3: Ancient Egypt
am-os-egypt.notes: Early monarchy, Nile ecology and Old/Middle Kingdom sequences. Broad synthesis.

am-met-egypt-old.title: Tara Prakash, Egypt in the Old Kingdom (Metropolitan Museum of Art)
am-met-egypt-old.notes: Old Kingdom royal organization and funerary evidence. Settlement evidence less abundant than elite funerary material.

am-met-egypt-middle.title: Egypt in the Middle Kingdom (Metropolitan Museum of Art)
am-met-egypt-middle.notes: Political reunification, literature and changing regional institutions. Collapse causes debated.

am-unesco-memphis.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Memphis and its Necropolis
am-unesco-memphis.notes: Giza and Saqqara monument locations and capital site history. Heritage inventory does not identify individual labor contracts.

am-aera-giza.title: Ancient Egypt Research Associates, The Lost City of the Pyramids (Heit el-Ghurab)
am-aera-giza.notes: Excavated pyramid-worker settlement and the material logistics of construction. Site-specific, not evidence that all Egyptian labor arrangements were identical.

am-os-newkingdom.title: OpenStax, World History Volume 1, section 4.2: Egypt’s New Kingdom
am-os-newkingdom.notes: New Kingdom expansion, Egyptian-Nubian relations and royal religion. Textbook synthesis; royal texts may be propaganda.

am-os-indus.title: OpenStax, World History Volume 1, section 3.4: The Indus Valley Civilization
am-os-indus.notes: Indus urban forms, seals and de-urbanization. Evidence cannot yet decode political titles or inhabitants’ language.

am-unesco-dholavira.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Dholavira: a Harappan City
am-unesco-dholavira.notes: Archaeology, urban layout, water systems, craft and settlement changes. Heritage synopsis not a definitive political reconstruction.

am-unesco-mohenjo.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Archaeological Ruins at Moenjodaro
am-unesco-mohenjo.notes: Urban planning, chronology and archaeology of major Indus site. Material remains alone cannot identify political offices.

am-nature-indus-drought.title: 2023 speleothem study, Recurring summer and winter droughts from 4.2–3.97 thousand years ago in north India (Communications Earth & Environment)
am-nature-indus-drought.notes: Local seasonal hydroclimate reconstruction. Cave precipitation proxies do not directly establish migration motives or a single civilization-wide collapse.

am-nature-indus-river.title: 2017 study, Counter-intuitive influence of Himalayan river morphodynamics on Indus Civilisation urban settlements (Nature Communications)
am-nature-indus-river.notes: Dating of palaeochannel and evidence against a contemporaneous perennial Himalayan-fed river along the studied Ghaggar–Hakra course. Regional study.

am-unesco-liangzhu.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Archaeological Ruins of Liangzhu City
am-unesco-liangzhu.notes: Lower Yangtze early state, rice cultivation, engineered waterworks and burials. Site-specific and heritage-focused.

am-os-china.title: OpenStax, World History Volume 1, section 5.1: Ancient China
am-os-china.notes: Neolithic diversity, Erlitou and Xia identification, Shang inscriptions, Zhou politics. Broad historical synthesis.

am-met-china-bronze.title: The Shang and Zhou Dynasties: The Bronze Age of China (Metropolitan Museum of Art)
am-met-china-bronze.notes: Shang and Zhou bronze craft and ritual traditions. High-status archaeological record.

am-met-china-time.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, China, 2000–1000 BCE (Heilbrunn Timeline)
am-met-china-time.notes: Erlitou, Anyang, Sanxingdui and Zhou political-artistic chronology. Regional museum synthesis.

am-ina-uluburun.title: Institute of Nautical Archaeology, Uluburun Late Bronze Age Shipwreck Excavation
am-ina-uluburun.notes: Wreck discovery, date, bulk metal cargo and interregional objects. One wreck does not prove itinerary or market structure.

am-unesco-hattusha.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Hattusha: the Hittite Capital
am-unesco-hattusha.notes: Hittite capital, fortifications, royal and ritual buildings. Heritage record not a complete diplomatic archive.

am-os-med.title: OpenStax, World History Volume 1, section 6.1: Early Mediterranean Peoples
am-os-med.notes: Late Bronze Age diplomacy, palace systems, trade and post-1200 transitions. Synthetic and some collapse mechanisms remain debated.

am-oxford-aegean.title: Guy D. Middleton, Collapse of the Bronze Age Aegean (Oxford Classical Dictionary, 2019)
am-oxford-aegean.notes: Aegean palace destructions and competing explanations; abstract reviewed, full article not independently read.

am-jarch-collapse.title: Collapse Studies in Archaeology from 2012 to 2023 (Journal of Archaeological Research, 2024)
am-jarch-collapse.notes: Comparative research review of diverse definitions and hypotheses for eastern Mediterranean collapse. Review, not a single event report.

am-unesco-caral.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Sacred City of Caral-Supe
am-unesco-caral.notes: Caral architecture, Supe Valley setting and third-millennium chronology. UNESCO state-designation language can overstate certainty about political form.

am-met-olmec.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Olmec Art
am-met-olmec.notes: San Lorenzo, colossal heads, La Venta, Mesoamerican art networks and undeciphered writing. Art evidence is not a roster of rulers.

am-os-americas.title: OpenStax, World History Volume 1, section 8.1: Populating and Settling the Americas
am-os-americas.notes: Independent agriculture, varied regional systems, Supe monumental centers and Eastern Woodlands. Generalized chronology carries local uncertainty.

am-met-phoenicians.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Phoenicians (1500-300 B.C.)
am-met-phoenicians.notes: Coastal city histories, craft, trade and alphabetic diffusion; the label Phoenician comes from later outsiders and city politics differed.

am-met-alphabet.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Alphabet Origins: From Kipling to Sinai
am-met-alphabet.notes: Origins before 1200 BCE and later Mediterranean transmission; surviving inscriptions cannot measure population-wide literacy.

am-met-greek-geometric.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Geometric Art in Ancient Greece
am-met-greek-geometric.notes: Geometric period, polis development, sanctuary and overseas settlement context; cultural synthesis rather than a household-level social history.

am-met-anatolia-time.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Anatolia and the Caucasus 1000 B.C.-1 A.D.
am-met-anatolia-time.notes: Iron Age state and regional chronology; broad overview, contested dynamics of migration and identity need more specialist evidence.

am-met-assyria-iberia.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Assyria to Iberia at the Dawn of the Classical Age
am-met-assyria-iberia.notes: Neo-Assyrian expansion, tribute, deportation and royal visual claims; exhibition synthesis, not a census of displaced populations.

am-met-levant-time.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Eastern Mediterranean and Syria 1000 B.C.-1 A.D.
am-met-levant-time.notes: Dated Levantine conquest, resettlement and later developments; regional event chronology rather than full social evidence.

am-lachish-reliefs.title: Lachish Archaeological Project, Lachish Battle Reliefs
am-lachish-reliefs.notes: 701 BCE campaign in Assyrian reliefs and relationship to excavated siege; reliefs favor their royal patron and cannot settle all casualty estimates.

am-met-esarhaddon.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Esarhaddon Prism Describing Restoration of Babylon
am-met-esarhaddon.notes: Primary cuneiform record of Esarhaddon royal restoration rhetoric after Sennacherib; propaganda, not independent diagnosis of responsibility.

am-met-achaemenid.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Achaemenid Persian Empire (550-330 B.C.)
am-met-achaemenid.notes: Broad chronology of Cyrus, Cambyses, Darius, palace art and satrapies; survey synthesizes diverse and sometimes disputed evidence.

am-met-cyrus-cylinder.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Cyrus Cylinder and Ancient Persia
am-met-cyrus-cylinder.notes: Cyrus Cylinder text and context of Babylonian conquest; royal foundation narrative, not a universal human-rights charter.

am-iranica-persepolis-tablets.title: Muhammad A. Dandamayev, Persepolis Elamite Tablets, Encyclopaedia Iranica
am-iranica-persepolis-tablets.notes: Fortification and Treasury archives, dates, provisioning and seal impressions; mostly records of specific Iranian heartland institutions.

am-iranica-bisotun.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica, Bisotun III: Darius's Inscriptions
am-iranica-bisotun.notes: Details of the trilingual Bisotun royal inscription; Darius frames political opponents as liars and legitimates conquest.

am-hyland-admin.title: John O. Hyland, Achaemenid Administration (2021)
am-hyland-admin.notes: Specialist overview of itinerant court and satrapal administration using Persepolis records; only public abstract reviewed.

am-met-greece-time.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Ancient Greece 1000 B.C.-1 A.D.
am-met-greece-time.notes: Chronology of Greek poleis, settlements and political changes; survey cannot describe every local political system.

am-stanford-ancient-political.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Ancient Political Philosophy
am-stanford-ancient-political.notes: Citizenship, constitutional variety and Greek political debate; focused on intellectual history and elite textual sources.

am-stanford-aristotle.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Aristotle's Political Theory
am-stanford-aristotle.notes: Aristotle on citizenship and constitutions; late-fourth-century normative analysis, not a fifth-century population survey.

am-met-greek-classical.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Art of Classical Greece (ca. 480-323 B.C.)
am-met-greek-classical.notes: Athens and Delian League with classical culture chronology; Athenian and elite focus.

am-cambridge-metics.title: James Watson, The Origin of Metic Status at Athens (2010)
am-cambridge-metics.notes: Debates the date at which metic legal status formed; public extract supports uncertainty, not a settled new consensus.

am-cambridge-mahajanapada.title: A. D. H. Bivar, The Indus Lands, Cambridge Ancient History
am-cambridge-mahajanapada.notes: Sixth-century BCE north Indian states and Magadha; extract from scholarly synthesis, dependent on layered early sources.

am-met-southasia-time.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, South Asia 1000 B.C.-1 A.D.
am-met-southasia-time.notes: Regional chronology of early cities, ceramic traditions, Buddhist and Jain thought; some older dates differ from current specialist reconstructions.

am-stanford-buddha.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Buddha (revised 2023)
am-stanford-buddha.notes: Historical Buddha chronology, shramana setting and uncertainty of texts transmitted in later recensions.

am-stanford-jaina.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Jaina Philosophy (2023)
am-stanford-jaina.notes: Mahavira in Jain traditions, ahimsa, renunciation and textual transmission; a history of traditions, not eyewitness biography.

am-met-zhou-time.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, China 1000 B.C.-1 A.D.
am-met-zhou-time.notes: Eastern Zhou, Spring and Autumn, Warring States chronology and material culture; period boundaries conventional.

am-stanford-chinese-political.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Social and Political Thought in Chinese Philosophy
am-stanford-chinese-political.notes: Early Chinese ethical and administrative debates and layered texts; philosophical account, not direct evidence of daily state policies.

am-stanford-mohism.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Mohism
am-stanford-mohism.notes: Inclusive care, opposition to aggressive war, and Mohist textual history; disputed interpretation of ethical demands.

am-stanford-confucius.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Confucius (2022 archive)
am-stanford-confucius.notes: Ritual and governance ideas attributed to Confucius; Analects is a later compilation with multiple layers.

am-met-egypt-thirdintermediate.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Egypt in the Third Intermediate Period (ca. 1070-664 B.C.)
am-met-egypt-thirdintermediate.notes: Piye, Nubian Twenty-fifth Dynasty and Assyrian intervention; Egyptian-centered chronology has limits for Nubian local life.

am-unesco-kush-meroe.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Archaeological Sites of the Island of Meroe
am-unesco-kush-meroe.notes: Long continuity of Kush and Meroe architecture and production; Meroe flourished over later centuries, not all sites date to 700 BCE.

am-met-sudan-time.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Sudan 1000 B.C.-1 A.D.
am-met-sudan-time.notes: Napatan and Meroitic chronology, royal sites and regional trade; overview focused on visible elite material evidence.

am-smarthistory-piye.title: British Museum, King Piye and the Kushite Control of Egypt (Smarthistory)
am-smarthistory-piye.notes: Piye Victory Stela and Kushite authority in Egypt; first-person victory rhetoric is not neutral evidence of motives.

am-tichitt-2026.title: Revisiting Tichitt: New Dates and Data from the 1968 Excavations (2026)
am-tichitt-2026.notes: New radiocarbon analysis of stone-walled settlement excavations in Mauritania; chronological revisions reveal limits of earlier conventional dating.

am-oxford-nok.title: Gabriele Franke, The Archaeology of Nok Culture in Nigeria (2024)
am-oxford-nok.notes: Nok settlements, terracotta, dated iron evidence and lack of demonstrated central state; abstract only, with limits on local variability.

am-cambridge-jenne.title: The Inland Niger Delta Before the Empire of Mali: Evidence from Jenne-jeno, Journal of African History
am-cambridge-jenne.notes: Jenne-jeno occupation from third century BCE and urban expansion much later; abstract and survey summary, not a complete excavation publication.

am-met-mexico-time.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Mexico 1000 B.C.-1 A.D.
am-met-mexico-time.notes: Chronology of Olmec, Monte Alban, Cuicuilco and Teotihuacan; avoid extending later city sizes backward.

am-met-montealban.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Monte Alban
am-met-montealban.notes: Foundation around 500 BCE, regional organization and later growth; political interpretations are inferential.

am-unesco-chavin.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Chavin (Archaeological Site)
am-unesco-chavin.notes: Ceremonial terraces, galleries and regional influence; religious reach is not proof of territorial empire.

am-smarthistory-chavin.title: Sarahh Scher, Chavin de Huantar, Smarthistory (2015)
am-smarthistory-chavin.notes: Temple phases and ritual architectural features; interpretation of ancient experience cannot be observed directly.

am-met-paracas.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Paracas Border Fragment, Figures with Staves
am-met-paracas.notes: Fourth to third century BCE surviving embroidered textile and broader Paracas fiber traditions; funerary bias.

am-met-northamerica-time.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, North America 1000 B.C.-1 A.D.
am-met-northamerica-time.notes: Eastern Woodlands Adena ceremonial and North American Arctic/Southwest chronologies; generalized regional overview.

am-met-andes-time.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Central and Southern Andes 1000 B.C.-1 A.D.
am-met-andes-time.notes: Regional Andes ceremonial centers and Paracas chronology; broad comparative dates vary by specialist and site.

am-cam-hellenistic.title: M. M. Austin, The Hellenistic World from Alexander to the Roman Conquest, 2nd ed., Cambridge University Press, introduction
am-cam-hellenistic.notes: Source-method overview of dynastic fragmentation, varied local institutions, non-Greek continuity and surviving literary/papyrological evidence. Cambridge excerpt pp. 1-5 reviewed; not the complete book.

am-met-alexander.title: Colette and Sean Hemingway, The Rise of Macedon and the Conquests of Alexander the Great, Metropolitan Museum of Art
am-met-alexander.notes: Alexander campaign chronology and later succession. Museum synthesis; precise individual motives and anecdotal details depend on later narrative histories.

am-met-hellenistic.title: Colette and Sean Hemingway, Art of the Hellenistic Age and the Hellenistic Tradition, Metropolitan Museum of Art
am-met-hellenistic.notes: Successor dynasties, royal artistic patronage, regional diversity and long cultural interchange. Art objects do not alone establish population-wide language or identity.

am-met-seleucid.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Seleucid Empire (323-64 B.C.)
am-met-seleucid.notes: Seleucid dynastic geography, political change and mixed artistic forms. Geographic reach fluctuated and must not imply uniform local compliance.

am-met-ptolemy.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Nile and Newcomers: A Fresh Installation of Egyptian Ptolemaic Art
am-met-ptolemy.notes: Ptolemaic Egyptian temples, Greek-speaking royal court, shifting social hierarchies, interaction of local traditions. Museum art orientation.

am-ox-zenon.title: Oxford Academic, Money and Prices in the Papyri, Ptolemaic Period
am-ox-zenon.notes: Zenon estate archive, third-century BCE Fayum and countryside documentation, royal land and estate economy. Papyri are geographically and socially selective.

am-met-maurya.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Mauryan Empire (ca. 323-185 B.C.)
am-met-maurya.notes: Chandragupta, Bindusara, Ashoka, Mauryan geographic chronology and monuments. Some traditional Arthashastra attribution is simplified in this overview.

am-ox-thapar-ashoka.title: Romila Thapar, Inscriptions as Historical Writing in Early India, Oxford History of Historical Writing
am-ox-thapar-ashoka.notes: Ashokan Prakrit, Greek, Aramaic languages and Brahmi, Kharoshthi, Greek, Aramaic scripts; inscriptions as historically situated royal statements. Abstract only.

am-cam-ashoka-geography.title: Monica L. Smith et al., Finding History: The Locational Geography of Ashokan Inscriptions, Antiquity 90 (2016)
am-cam-ashoka-geography.notes: Location and distribution of Ashokan inscriptions, political geography and demographic uncertainty; abstract does not establish universal policy enforcement.

am-ashoka-rock13.title: Vincent A. Smith, Asoka: The Buddhist Emperor of India, translated Rock Edict XIII and accompanying notes (public-domain edition)
am-ashoka-rock13.notes: Rock Edict XIII including Kalinga, royal figures for deaths and deportation and language of remorse. Old translation; numbers are not independently corroborated counts and translation choices vary.

am-bm-ashoka.title: British Museum collection, Ashokan Major Pillar Edict VI fragment (1880,21)
am-bm-ashoka.notes: Material fragment from an Ashokan inscribed pillar; object attests monumental inscription production, not empire-wide uptake of royal directives.

am-ucla-arthashastra.title: UCLA MANAS, Kautilya and Arthashastra
am-ucla-arthashastra.notes: Artashastra text is composite and not a descriptive administrative ledger from Chandragupta; traditional attribution disputed.

am-met-han.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Han Dynasty (206 B.C.-220 A.D.)
am-met-han.notes: Han reunification, chronology, Chang-an, Emperor Wu, frontiers, Sima Qian and intellectual activity; overview emphasizes elite and court perspectives.

am-cam-qin-law.title: Li Jingrong and Chen Songchang, The Promulgation of Law in Qin and Western Han China, Early China
am-cam-qin-law.notes: Excavated laws, uneven distribution to offices, courier delays and local administrative practice. Abstract only.

am-uc-qin-records.title: Birth of an Empire: The State of Qin Revisited, University of California eScholarship
am-uc-qin-records.notes: Qin and Han household registers, tax/conscript records from Liye and other sites; source evidence uneven and dependent on excavation context.

am-stanford-legalism.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Legalism in Chinese Philosophy
am-stanford-legalism.notes: Warring States governing doctrines and later Han portrayals of Qin policy, legal texts and political interpretation; not a chronicle of every court event.

am-unesco-qin.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Mausoleum of the First Qin Emperor
am-unesco-qin.notes: Terracotta complex, date, physical evidence of labor organization and craft; later labor numbers attributed to Sima Qian require source caution.

am-met-rome-republic.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Roman Republic
am-met-rome-republic.notes: Roman republican institutions, Italian expansion, political conflict, provincial conquest, Caesar and civil war; survey periodizes differently from local histories.

am-met-rome-empire.title: Christopher S. Lightfoot, The Roman Empire (27 B.C.-393 A.D.), Metropolitan Museum of Art
am-met-rome-empire.notes: Augustan principate and imperial administration, frontier and provincial rule; elite-centered broad overview.

am-met-roman-egypt.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Roman Egypt
am-met-roman-egypt.notes: Conquest and administration of Egypt after 30 BCE, local obligations and interaction of traditions; limited for conditions of other Roman provinces.

am-ox-slavery-egypt.title: Jane Rowlandson, Creating a Slave Society? The Greek and Roman Impact on Egypt, Oxford Handbook of Greek and Roman Slaveries
am-ox-slavery-egypt.notes: Variation and transformations in slavery and dependency in Ptolemaic and Roman Egypt; abstract only, not quantitative empire-wide slave census.

am-cam-romanwomen.title: Emily A. Hemelrijk, Legal Status, Citizenship and Ethnicity, Women and Society in the Roman World, Cambridge
am-cam-romanwomen.notes: Women slaves, freedwomen, foreign-born women, legal status and funerary inscriptions; inscriptions skew toward those represented in commemoration.

am-ox-babatha.title: Kimberley Czajkowski, Babatha, Oxford Classical Dictionary / Oxford Research Encyclopedia
am-ox-babatha.notes: Second-century documents, property and litigation near Dead Sea, Roman Arabia and local legal pluralism; wealthy-person archive not representative of all households.

am-met-sudan500.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Sudan 1-500 A.D.
am-met-sudan500.notes: Meroitic Kush, early CE trade, artifacts and broad chronology; generalized Nile-centered timeline.

am-unesco-aksum.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Aksum
am-unesco-aksum.notes: Aksumite rise, highland and Red Sea connections, later monumental evidence; do not project later fourth-century Christianity into first-century states.

am-met-ctesiphon.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Ctesiphon
am-met-ctesiphon.notes: Parthian and Sasanian political center on the Tigris, Roman attacks and 224 CE transition; city history not entire Iranian realm.

am-met-kushan.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Kushan Empire (ca. Second Century B.C.-Third Century A.D.)
am-met-kushan.notes: Yuezhi/Kushan movement, central and southern Asian geography, trade and Buddhist artistic exchange; dynasty dates and territorial extent debated.

am-met-gandhara.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Gandhara
am-met-gandhara.notes: Buddhist institutions and reliquary inscription of Indravarman, local patronage, material and artistic exchange. Do not conflate style with identity.

am-met-iran500.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Iran 1-500 A.D.
am-met-iran500.notes: Parthian and Sasanian chronology and trade contexts; survey uses broad political labels.

am-unesco-silk.title: UNESCO, About the Silk Roads
am-unesco-silk.notes: Modern invention of Silk Road label, plural overland and maritime networks, diverse cargo and ideas; spans many centuries, not specific transaction records.

am-met-romasia.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Trade between the Romans and the Empires of Asia
am-met-romasia.notes: Han, Xiongnu, Kushan, Parthian and Roman exchanges, monsoon navigation and intermediaries; synthesis cannot prove all individual itineraries.

am-athens-periplus.title: Dimitris Plantzos, Introduction to the Periplus of the Red Sea, University of Athens
am-athens-periplus.notes: Dating, Greek maritime guide, Red Sea and western Indian Ocean ports; unnamed author gives merchant-oriented partial geographic coverage.

am-ox-berenike.title: Steven E. Sidebotham, Trade in Roman Berenike, Berenike and the Ancient Maritime Spice Route, Oxford Academic
am-ox-berenike.notes: Excavated black pepper, Indian Ocean materials and cautions against equating Roman coins in India with exact trade balance. Abstract only.

am-met-teotihuacan.title: Trenton Barnes, Teotihuacan, Metropolitan Museum of Art (2024)
am-met-teotihuacan.notes: City development, monuments 100-250 CE, apartment compounds after ca. 250 CE, urban form and diverse inhabitants; later peak size not transferable backward.

am-met-mexico500.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Mexico 1-500 A.D.
am-met-mexico500.notes: Early classical central Mexican and Oaxaca chronology; dated events in later fifth centuries lie outside opening focus.

am-unesco-sanbartolo.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, The Painted Murals of San Bartolo (tentative list)
am-unesco-sanbartolo.notes: Maya Preclassic painted murals ca. 100 BCE, religious scenes and writing; mythological interpretation depends on comparisons with later traditions.

am-pnas-sanbartolo.title: David Stuart et al., An Early Maya Calendar Record from San Bartolo, Guatemala, Science Advances (2022)
am-pnas-sanbartolo.notes: Radiocarbon-supported early Maya calendar date and early scripts at San Bartolo; does not describe all Maya political arrangements.

am-cam-maya-lidar.title: Richard D. Hansen et al., LiDAR Analyses in the Mirador-Calakmul Karst Basin, Ancient Mesoamerica (2022)
am-cam-maya-lidar.notes: Preclassic Maya settlements, causeways, geographic scope and potential interactions; site hierarchy and political interpretation remain analytical inferences.

am-unesco-nasca.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Lines and Geoglyphs of Nasca and Palpa
am-unesco-nasca.notes: Multiple geoglyph phases from centuries BCE to 500 CE, methods and possible rituals. Functions remain debated.

am-met-moche.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Moche Decorated Ceramics
am-met-moche.notes: Moche north coast irrigation, labor tribute, ceramics and ritual imagery, first to eighth centuries CE; pictorial scenes not direct dated chronicles.

am-met-andes500.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Central and Southern Andes 1-500 A.D.
am-met-andes500.notes: Regional Andean societies and early centuries CE pottery, irrigation and Nasca/Moche chronologies; generalized dates.

am-nps-hopewell.title: US National Park Service, Hopewell Culture National Historical Park: History and Culture
am-nps-hopewell.notes: Hopewell-period earthworks, exchange materials, regional links and archaeological naming; no evidence of empire equivalent to Teotihuacan.

am-unesco-montealban.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Historic Centre of Oaxaca and Archaeological Site of Monte Alban
am-unesco-montealban.notes: Monte Alban long chronology, monuments, Zapotec history and changing significance; names and political functions not always directly legible.

am-nps-hopewell-interpret.title: US National Park Service, Hopewell Earthworks
am-nps-hopewell-interpret.notes: Hopewell terminology is archaeological modern designation, not native self-name; later colonial displacement shaped research context.

am-met-byzantium.title: Department of Medieval Art, Byzantium (ca. 330–1453), Metropolitan Museum of Art
am-met-byzantium.notes: Eastern Roman continuity; capital, Christianity, western territorial changes and seventh-century losses. Broad survey; does not establish conditions in every province.

am-met-justinian.title: Department of Medieval Art, The Byzantine State under Justinian I, Metropolitan Museum of Art
am-met-justinian.notes: Justinian 527–565, Nika uprising, Hagia Sophia, reconquests, imperial legal compilation. Royal/palace perspective; casualties and impacts on local populations require caution.

am-unesco-ravenna.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Early Christian Monuments of Ravenna
am-unesco-ravenna.notes: Surviving Ostrogothic and eastern Roman fifth–sixth-century churches, mosaics, Ravenna political chronology; curated monument selection not a social survey.

am-ox-justinian-plague.title: New Approaches to the Plague of Justinian, Past & Present (2022)
am-ox-justinian-plague.notes: Sixth-century epidemic testimony across regions and the debated scale and causal effects; demographic figures in narrative sources cannot be assumed precise.

am-goettingen-byz-law.title: Göttingen Academy of Sciences, Byzantine Legal Sources Research Centre
am-goettingen-byz-law.notes: Justinianic legal collection, later Byzantine Greek translations and manuscript tradition; survival and study of law do not prove province-wide enforcement.

am-met-byz-islam.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Byzantium and Islam: Age of Transition exhibition scholarship
am-met-byz-islam.notes: Chalcedonian disputes, non-Chalcedonian communities, early seventh/eighth-century transformations. Focus on eastern Mediterranean religious and material evidence.

am-cam-egypt-change.title: Roger S. Bagnall, The Persians, the Arab Conquest, and Another Transformation of Egypt, Roman Egypt, Cambridge
am-cam-egypt-change.notes: Seventh-century Persian and Arab conquests and continuity/change of Egyptian local elites, Coptic and Greek. Chapter summary only; Egyptian pattern not universal.

am-met-sasanian.title: Blair Fowlkes-Childs and Department of Ancient Near Eastern Art, The Sasanian Empire (224–651), Metropolitan Museum of Art
am-met-sasanian.notes: Dynastic overview, Shapur and Roman wars, royal reliefs, Ctesiphon, silver and textile art and trade. Museum summary simplifies Zoroastrian state-religion chronology.

am-iranica-sasanian.title: Alireza Shapur Shahbazi, Sasanian Dynasty, Encyclopaedia Iranica
am-iranica-sasanian.notes: Ardashir 224, succession, aristocracy, royal ideology and political changes; later written sources require source criticism, and royal religious centralization is contested.

am-iranica-fiscal.title: Rika Gyselen, Fiscal System ii. Sasanian, Encyclopaedia Iranica
am-iranica-fiscal.notes: Evidence limitations for taxes, land revenues, dependence on later Arabic historians and Pahlavi/Syriac records; few direct fiscal archives survive.

am-iranica-khosrow.title: Zeev Rubin, Khosrow I ii. Reforms, Encyclopaedia Iranica
am-iranica-khosrow.notes: Tax and military reforms under Kavad I and Khosrow I; details principally reported by later literary sources, not contemporary tax ledgers.

am-iranica-christians.title: Judith A. Lerner, Christianity ii. In Pre-Islamic Persia: Material Remains, Encyclopaedia Iranica
am-iranica-christians.notes: Material traces of Christian communities in Sasanian lands; limited archaeology and geographical coverage.

am-iranica-iran.title: Encyclopaedia Iranica, Iran ii. Iranian History (1): Pre-Islamic Times
am-iranica-iran.notes: Religious plurality and conflicts, Roman-Iranian relations, the final dynasty; scholarly synthesis but some terms reflect older historical terminology.

am-cam-south-arabia.title: Valentina A. Grasso, The Shape of the Sixth Century I: The South, Pre-Islamic Arabia, Cambridge (2023)
am-cam-south-arabia.notes: Najran 523, Himyar and Aksum political-religious conflicts and Abraha; summary emphasizes contested economic and religious motives; full chapter not reviewed.

am-cam-gupta-archeo.title: Grounding Texts and Theories of Societal Change, Antiquity (2022)
am-cam-gupta-archeo.notes: Gupta and Vakataka states, land grants, material evidence and problematic golden-age/early-medieval categories; geographic and methodological specificity.

am-cam-samudragupta.title: Royal Asiatic Society, Samudra Gupta and his Prayagraj/Allahabad pillar inscription, Journal of the Royal Asiatic Society (1897)
am-cam-samudragupta.notes: Early scholarly description of Samudragupta pillar panegyric and Harishena attribution; nineteenth-century interpretation is not current consensus on chronology.

am-met-southasia500.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, South Asia, 1–500 A.D. chronology
am-met-southasia500.notes: Gupta-era politics, Gupta religious art and Vakataka Ajanta patronage; broad art-focused dates.

am-unesco-ajanta.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Ajanta Caves
am-unesco-ajanta.notes: Two main phases of Ajanta Buddhist cave building and Vakataka fifth/sixth-century patronage; does not represent all Gupta-era South Asian regions.

am-met-buddhism-art.title: Vidya Dehejia, Buddhism and Buddhist Art, Metropolitan Museum of Art
am-met-buddhism-art.notes: Regional Buddhist image-making and Gupta-period sculptural styles. Art history scope; religious experience cannot be inferred uniformly.

am-cam-gupta-interactions.title: The Importance of Gupta-period Sculpture in Southeast Asian Art History, Cambridge
am-cam-gupta-interactions.notes: Gupta dynasty ca. 320–500 and cross-regional visual borrowing; abstract explicitly questions older assumptions about artistic influence.

am-met-northern-southern.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Period of Northern and Southern Dynasties (386–581)
am-met-northern-southern.notes: Northern Wei, Southern courts, Buddhist caves, Emperor Xiaowen and migration. Period synthesis uses broad, sometimes dated ethnicity labels.

am-unesco-yungang.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Yungang Grottoes
am-unesco-yungang.notes: Imperial Northern Wei-sponsored Buddhist caves and South/Central Asian artistic interactions; high-status monument record.

am-unesco-longmen.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Longmen Grottoes
am-unesco-longmen.notes: Late Northern Wei and early Tang cave carving and inscriptions at Luoyang; material record not a population-wide faith survey.

am-met-china500.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, China, 500–1000 A.D., Heilbrunn Timeline
am-met-china500.notes: Sui reunification 581/589, Tang rise 618, canal, court culture and regional relationships; broad overview.

am-cam-coptic-syriac.title: Karel C. Innemée, Lucas Van Rompay, Dobrochna Zielinska, Church of the Virgin at Dayr al-Suryan, Cambridge Worlds of Byzantium (2024)
am-cam-coptic-syriac.notes: Coptic and Syriac monastic contact and changing material practices; the documented eighth-century contact should not be backdated to the fourth.

am-yale-councils.title: Yale University Library, Early Christianity and Patristics: Synods, Councils, and Orders research guide
am-yale-councils.notes: Identifies editions of Nicaea-to-Chalcedon council materials; guide to primary editions, not independent confirmation of each doctrinal argument.

am-met-islam-birth.title: Suzan Yalman after Linda Komaroff, The Birth of Islam, Metropolitan Museum of Art
am-met-islam-birth.notes: Muhammad, hijra, Quran, and first caliphates in a broad introductory chronology; traditional narratives are synthesized rather than independently verified.

am-met-muhammad.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Prophet Muhammad and the Origins of Islam, educational resource
am-met-muhammad.notes: Traditional biography and Muslim theological framing, Khadija, Medina, religious practice; specific speeches and motives reflect later transmitted sources.

am-birmingham-quran.title: University of Birmingham, Birmingham Qur’an Manuscript FAQ, Cadbury Research Library
am-birmingham-quran.notes: Surahs 18–20 and parchment radiocarbon range 568–645 (95.4%); test dates animal skin, not ink, composition, or original oral recitation.

am-cam-sinai-quran.title: Nicolai Sinai, When Did the Consonantal Skeleton of the Qur’an Reach Closure? Part II, Bulletin of SOAS (2014)
am-cam-sinai-quran.notes: Argument for early standard Quranic rasm against later eighth-century composition hypothesis; scholarly inference rather than proof of every traditional report.

am-cam-quran-bible.title: The Qur’an and the Bible, New Cambridge History of the Bible, Cambridge
am-cam-quran-bible.notes: Early Quranic corpus, late antique religious context and textual formation; abstract-only scope; contested reconstruction.

am-met-umayyad.title: Suzan Yalman after Linda Komaroff, The Art of the Umayyad Period (661–750), Metropolitan Museum of Art
am-met-umayyad.notes: First caliphs, Umayyad political change 661–750, Damascus and Dome of the Rock; emphasis on architecture and art and broad traditional chronology.

am-cam-coptic-tax.title: Scribal Networks, Taxation, and the Role of Coptic in Marwanid Egypt, Cambridge
am-cam-coptic-tax.notes: Greek/Coptic/Arabic Egypt documents and post-conquest tax and labor demands; regional specific, chapter summary only.

am-cam-nonmuslims.title: Non-Muslims in the Early Islamic Empire, conclusion, Cambridge
am-cam-nonmuslims.notes: Regional variation of initial surrender and tax arrangements; later Muslim reports of treaties should not be treated as unmediated documents of the 630s.

am-cam-islamisation.title: Harry Munt, What Did Conversion to Islam Mean in Seventh-Century Arabia?, Islamisation, Cambridge (2026)
am-cam-islamisation.notes: Middle Eastern conversions after conquests generally gradual over centuries; Arabian trajectory differs and remains debated. Summary only.

am-met-dome-rock.title: Ana Botchkareva, The Dome of the Rock, Metropolitan Museum of Art (2012)
am-met-dome-rock.notes: Jerusalem monument construction 688–692 and multireligious setting; later interpretations of the rock do not establish original eighth-century intent.

am-cam-dome-inscription.title: Sheila Blair and Jonathan Bloom, Inscriptions in Art and Architecture, Cambridge Companion to the Qur’an
am-cam-dome-inscription.notes: Dome of the Rock early Quranic inscription completed 692; summary not an edition of each inscription.

am-met-aksum-found.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Foundations of Aksumite Civilization and Its Christian Legacy
am-met-aksum-found.notes: Aksum–Adulis trade, coinage, Ezana and Christianity, later political changes; older simplified causal account of trade decline is contested.

am-met-aksum-stelae.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Monumental Stelae of Aksum (3rd–4th Century)
am-met-aksum-stelae.notes: Aksum stelae form, archaeology and royal burials; workers and exact ritual interpretations not directly known.

am-met-aksum-architecture.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Monumental Architecture and Stelae of the Aksumite Empire
am-met-aksum-architecture.notes: King Ezana, coins with crosses, multilingual royal texts and long-distance messaging; elite evidence does not date all local conversions.

am-met-african-christ.title: Emma George Ross, African Christianity in Ethiopia, Metropolitan Museum of Art
am-met-african-christ.notes: Fourth-century Ezana and Frumentius tradition, Ethiopian church and Alexandria connection; narrative based on later ecclesiastical historians.

am-cam-adulis.title: Gabriele Castiglia, An Archaeology of Conversion? Evidence from Adulis, Antiquity (2022)
am-cam-adulis.notes: Adulis sixth/early seventh century church structures and dating; site-specific excavation, abstract rather than full article.

mw-os-abbasids.title: OpenStax, World History Volume 1, 11.3, Islamization and Religious Rule under Islam
mw-os-abbasids.notes: Abbasid revolution, foundation and administration of Baghdad, mixed communities, translation and legal traditions; general survey, not original documents.

mw-met-abbasid.title: Suzan Yalman after Linda Komaroff, Art of the Abbasid Period, Metropolitan Museum of Art
mw-met-abbasid.notes: Abbasid Baghdad 762, Samarra 836–892, art and political fragmentation; art history and court chronology are not a survey of village life.

mw-cam-translation.title: L. E. Goodman, Translation of Greek Materials into Arabic, in Religion, Learning and Science in the Abbasid Period, Cambridge
mw-cam-translation.notes: Arabic and earlier Syriac translations; learned communities and cross-cultural transmission; online summary, not full chapter.

mw-cam-hunayn.title: Coleman Connelly, Hunayn ibn Ishaq’s Conception of His Reading Public, Arabic Sciences and Philosophy 2020
mw-cam-hunayn.notes: Editions of a translator’s letter and Syriac Christian patronage; abstract only, no license for sweeping claims about all Baghdad translators.

mw-cam-zanj.title: Peter J. Brown et al., Landscape of the Zanj Rebellion? Antiquity 2025
mw-cam-zanj.notes: Zanj revolt 869–883, interpretation and new dating of southern Iraqi agricultural earthworks; dated earthworks do not identify builders or rebellion participants.

mw-os-seljuk.title: OpenStax, World History Volume 1, 13.2, The Seljuk Migration and the Call from the East
mw-os-seljuk.notes: Abbasid fragmentation and relationships with Seljuk authorities; secondary overview simplifies regional differences.

mw-met-tang.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Tang Dynasty (618–907)
mw-met-tang.notes: Tang court history, Chang’an, cultural and international contacts; court focus and celebratory dynasty framing require balance.

mw-met-tang-international.title: Heather Colburn Clydesdale, Internationalism in the Tang Dynasty, Metropolitan Museum of Art
mw-met-tang-international.notes: Imported goods, cross-border exchanges and representations of foreigners; art cannot census all communities.

mw-cam-song-econ.title: Joseph P. McDermott and Shiba Yoshinobu, Economic Change in China, 960–1279, Cambridge History of China
mw-cam-song-econ.notes: Regional variation in Song demographic, agricultural and market changes; only chapter summary reviewed.

mw-cam-song-society.title: Robert Hymes, Sung Society and Social Change, Cambridge History of China
mw-cam-song-society.notes: Song commercial economy, market relations and printing; chapter summary, not proof that all people benefited equally.

mw-cam-song-state.title: Charles Hartman, Sung Government and Politics, Cambridge History of China
mw-cam-song-state.notes: Song state politics and examination institutions; only introductory text reviewed.

mw-cam-song-econ-revolution.title: An Economic Revolution?, Middle Imperial China 900–1350, Cambridge
mw-cam-song-econ-revolution.notes: Song commercialization, specialized production and paper money; question mark signals ongoing historiographical debates.

mw-met-chola.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, South Asia: South, 1000–1400 A.D.
mw-met-chola.notes: Chola temple construction, Rajaraja and Rajendra, bronze images and 11th-century Srivijaya campaign; regional court and artwork emphasis.

mw-cam-srivijaya.title: Philippe Beaujard, Southeast Asia: Rise of Srivijayan Thalassocracy and the Javanese Kingdoms
mw-cam-srivijaya.notes: Sriwijaya, inscriptions, Yijing, regional maritime power; partial chapter summary, not a map of exact territorial control.

mw-cam-srivijaya-late.title: Philippe Beaujard, Southeast Asia: From the Decline of Srivijaya to Mojopahit
mw-cam-srivijaya-late.notes: Changing eleventh- to thirteenth-century sea routes, Khmer and Chola interactions; summary only.

mw-unesco-borobudur.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Borobudur Temple Compounds
mw-unesco-borobudur.notes: Eighth–ninth-century Java Buddhist monument, reliefs and sacred interpretation; monument record not evidence for all rural life.

mw-unesco-angkor.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Angkor
mw-unesco-angkor.notes: Ninth–fifteenth century Khmer capitals, temples, reservoirs, canals and settlement landscape; no basis for a single-cause hydraulic determinism.

mw-os-maritime.title: OpenStax, World History Volume 1, 12.2, East-West Interactions in the Early Middle Ages
mw-os-maritime.notes: Early medieval trade, religion and maritime networks between South and Southeast Asia; broad textbook synthesis.

mw-ox-ghana.title: Nikolas Gestrich, The Empire of Ghana, Oxford Research Encyclopedia of African History
mw-ox-ghana.notes: Arabic accounts of Ghana from ninth century and deep uncertainty about political geography, Kumbi Saleh and Wagadu; abstract only.

mw-ox-middle-niger.title: Roderick J. McIntosh, Urbanization in the Middle Niger of Mali, Oxford Research Encyclopedia
mw-ox-middle-niger.notes: Jenne-Jeno heterarchical urban clustering and locally developed settlement; author abstract, not a complete site excavation report.

mw-cam-jenne.title: Roderick J. and Susan Keech McIntosh, Inland Niger Delta before Mali, Journal of African History
mw-cam-jenne.notes: Early excavations and growth of Jenne-Jeno in first millennium; dated 1981 paper and excerpt, later interpretations should be consulted too.

mw-unesco-djenne.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Old Towns of Djenné
mw-unesco-djenne.notes: Jenne-Jeno, regional floodplain setting and medieval commercial development; modern UNESCO site history must not be merged with early settlement uncritically.

mw-cam-swahili-clay.title: Traces of Clay: Exploring Slave and Migrant Identities in Medieval Swahili Zanzibar, Cambridge Archaeological Journal
mw-cam-swahili-clay.notes: Early coastal African settlements, fishing, Kiswahili as Bantu, local pottery and varying non-elite lives; specific excavations cannot describe all towns.

mw-nature-swahili.title: Entwined African and Asian Genetic Roots of Medieval Peoples of the Swahili Coast, Nature 2023
mw-nature-swahili.notes: Ancient DNA of sampled thirteenth–eighteenth-century burials, evidence for earlier ancestry mixing around 1000; elite-skewed later sample with uncertain dating.

mw-unesco-kilwa.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani and Songo Mnara
mw-unesco-kilwa.notes: Kilwa settlement ninth century, eleventh-century mosque, later monumental growth; do not place thirteenth-century palace life in 900.

mw-os-medieval-europe.title: OpenStax, World History Volume 1, 13.1, Post-Roman West in the Early Middle Ages
mw-os-medieval-europe.notes: Carolingians, Christian institutions, land and dependent labor; textbook terms like feudalism may obscure local variation.

mw-cam-europe-trade.title: Derek Keene, Towns and the Growth of Trade, New Cambridge Medieval History
mw-cam-europe-trade.notes: Eleventh–twelfth century European urban growth with regional diversity and non-European connections; summary only.

mw-nationalarchives-domesday.title: UK National Archives, How to Look for Records of Domesday Book
mw-nationalarchives-domesday.notes: 1085–86 survey, land value, tenure, categories and record limits; describes government document rather than providing every original entry.

mw-os-crusades.title: OpenStax, World History Volume 1, Chapter 13 Introduction
mw-os-crusades.notes: Eleventh–twelfth-century religious and political conflicts including crusading; chapter overview is limited on affected Jewish, Muslim and eastern Christian communities.

mw-cam-rus-balkan.title: Cambridge, Byzantine Occupation of Bulgaria (963–1025), Byzantium’s Balkan Frontier
mw-cam-rus-balkan.notes: Rus dealings with Byzantium and Black Sea trade in the tenth century; regional Byzantine lens, summary only.

mw-unesco-lanse.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, L’Anse aux Meadows National Historic Site
mw-unesco-lanse.notes: Excavated short-lived eleventh-century Norse structures in Newfoundland; later saga attributions are not first-hand documentation.

mw-nature-norse1021.title: Margot Kuitems et al., Evidence for European Presence in the Americas in AD 1021, Nature 2021
mw-nature-norse1021.notes: Exact activity date derived from tree rings and 993 carbon anomaly at L’Anse aux Meadows; does not date each saga voyage.

mw-unesco-thingvellir.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Þingvellir National Park
mw-unesco-thingvellir.notes: Icelandic assembly conventionally founded 930, assembly and exclusion of unfree inhabitants; later history of site requires separate periodization.

mw-smithsonian-voyages.title: Smithsonian, Early Voyages, Time and Navigation
mw-smithsonian-voyages.notes: Norse and Polynesian open-water voyaging and environmental navigation; broad overview of methods, not a technical reconstruction of individual voyage.

mw-met-korea.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Korea, 500–1000 A.D., Heilbrunn Chronology
mw-met-korea.notes: Silla, Balhae, Goryeo, Buddhist patronage and political chronology; capital-focused elite account.

mw-met-heian.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Heian Period (794–1185)
mw-met-heian.notes: Japanese Heian court, Fujiwara families, kana and changing warrior power; elite focus.

mw-unesco-seokguram.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Seokguram Grotto and Bulguksa Temple
mw-unesco-seokguram.notes: Eighth-century Silla Buddhist construction, iconography and subsequent restoration; site-specific.

mw-met-genji.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Tale of Genji Exhibition Galleries
mw-met-genji.notes: Murasaki Shikibu and kana writing in Heian courtly culture; cannot treat literary fiction as direct record of all social groups.

mw-os-korea-japan.title: OpenStax, World History Volume 1, 12.3, Border States: Sogdiana, Korea, and Japan
mw-os-korea-japan.notes: Regional connections and changing political institutions; some textbook language implies over-simple Chinese diffusion.

mw-nature-polynesia.title: Paths and Timings of the Peopling of Polynesia Inferred from Genomic Networks, Nature 2021
mw-nature-polynesia.notes: Model for eastern Polynesian colonization sequences from modern genomic sampling; statistical inference, not confirmed date of every voyage.

mw-smithsonian-wayfinding.title: Smithsonian Institution, Early Voyages, Time and Navigation
mw-smithsonian-wayfinding.notes: Navigation by stars, currents and bird cues; broad overview and experimental reconstruction, not specific prehistoric eyewitness account.

mw-teara-aotearoa.title: Geoff Irwin and Carl Walrond, When Was New Zealand First Settled?, Te Ara Encyclopedia of New Zealand
mw-teara-aotearoa.notes: Evidence for Aotearoa first sustained settlement around 1250–1300 and problems with early rat-bone dates; later than 750–1200 focus.

mw-met-mongol-legacy.title: Qamar Adamjee and Stefano Carboni, The Legacy of Genghis Khan, Metropolitan Museum of Art
mw-met-mongol-legacy.notes: Mongol campaigns, successor states, institutional adaptation and elite artistic networks; art-historical synthesis, not a census of conquered subjects or independently quantified civilian losses.

mw-met-yuan-1271.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Yuan Dynasty (1271–1368)
mw-met-yuan-1271.notes: Yuan administration, dynastic chronology and material culture; court-centered synthesis, not comprehensive local social history.

mw-met-ilkhanid-art.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Art of the Ilkhanid Period (1256–1353)
mw-met-ilkhanid-art.notes: Ilkhanid Iran, Ghazan, art and interactions across Eurasia; visual and courtly emphasis does not establish the lives of all subjects.

mw-nature-plague-source.title: Maria A. Spyrou et al., The source of the Black Death in fourteenth-century central Eurasia, Nature 606 (2022)
mw-nature-plague-source.notes: Ancient DNA and 1338–1339 plague-related cemeteries in modern Kyrgyzstan; phylogenetic placement does not establish an exact path of movement or complete 14th-century regional mortality.

mw-cohn-postplague-labor.title: Samuel K. Cohn Jr., After the Black Death: labour legislation and attitudes towards labour in late-medieval western Europe, Economic History Review (2007)
mw-cohn-postplague-labor.notes: Comparative European labor legislation and responses to post-plague scarcity; conclusions are region-specific and do not provide a global mortality estimate.

mw-hopley-ibn-khaldun-plague.title: Russell Hopley, Plague, Demographic Upheaval and Civilisational Decline: Ibn Khaldun and the Black Death in the Maghreb, Landscapes (2016)
mw-hopley-ibn-khaldun-plague.notes: Ibn Khaldun and plague in the Maghreb; only bibliographic abstract checked, not independent verification of all specific medieval events.

mw-jmw-maghreb-plague.title: The Black Death in the Maghreb: A Call to Action, Journal of Medieval Worlds
mw-jmw-maghreb-plague.notes: North African plague historiography and major documentary gaps; explicitly warns against projecting European records onto other regions.

mw-met-west-central-sudan.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Western and Central Sudan, 1000–1400 A.D.
mw-met-west-central-sudan.notes: Political geography of medieval Sahel and Mali and regional artistic history; outsider written accounts and artifacts limit personal-level reconstruction.

mw-met-transsaharan-gold.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Trans-Saharan Gold Trade (7th–14th Century)
mw-met-transsaharan-gold.notes: Gold production and trade networks among West Africa, the Sahara and North Africa; cannot locate every source mine or reconstruct every caravan.

mw-unesco-timbuktu.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Timbuktu
mw-unesco-timbuktu.notes: Timbuktu material heritage, mosques and later traditions of Islamic learning; much of the best-documented manuscript culture and scholarship developed after Musa, so it should not be projected wholly into 1324.

mw-unesco-great-zimbabwe.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Great Zimbabwe National Monument
mw-unesco-great-zimbabwe.notes: Dry-stone architecture, 11th–15th-century settlement, farming and imported materials; heritage summary contains inherited legends not evidence for outsider construction.

mw-antiquity-zimbabwe-walls.title: Shadreck Chirikure and Innocent Pikirayi, Inside and outside the dry stone walls: revisiting the material culture of Great Zimbabwe, Antiquity (2008)
mw-antiquity-zimbabwe-walls.notes: Archaeological critique of simple social zoning based on surviving dry-stone walls; abstract, not a complete site-stratigraphic report.

mw-met-zimbabwe-art.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Great Zimbabwe (11th–15th Century)
mw-met-zimbabwe-art.notes: Shona ancestors, indigenous construction, trade objects and colonial misattributions; museum synthesis does not identify exact intentions of every wall or sculpture.

mw-cam-zimbabwe-colonial-labor.title: In the Shadows of Colonialism: Archaeological Labor Practices in (Post-)Colonial Zimbabwe, Advances in Archaeological Practice
mw-cam-zimbabwe-colonial-labor.notes: African labor and recognition in colonial/postcolonial archaeology; scholarly abstract, not a quantified history of every Great Zimbabwe excavation crew.

mw-met-tenochtitlan-early.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Tenochtitlan
mw-met-tenochtitlan-early.notes: Tenochtitlan founding traditions, water infrastructure, urban institutions, and Mexica expansion; later accounts must be cross-read with archaeology.

mw-met-maya-1400.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Maya Area, 1400–1600 A.D.
mw-met-maya-1400.notes: Mayapan and later northern Yucatán centers, K’iche’ and other highland polities; a regional chronology, not a primary K’iche’ text edition.

mw-met-maya-1000.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Maya Area, 1000–1400 A.D.
mw-met-maya-1000.notes: Later Maya city states and regional transformations; chronology is broad and archaeological interpretations remain debated.

mw-met-mexico-1400.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Mexico, 1400–1600 A.D.
mw-met-mexico-1400.notes: Mexica Triple Alliance, independent rivals, central Mexican art and politics; short regional synopsis does not document every tribute category.

mw-unesco-inca-roads.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Qhapaq Ñan, Andean Road System
mw-unesco-inca-roads.notes: Inca road network, pre-Inca road foundations, communications, infrastructure and state expansion; UNESCO composite listing is not a full study of individual labor systems.

mw-unesco-chan-chan.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Chan Chan Archaeological Zone
mw-unesco-chan-chan.notes: Chimú coastal center and adobe architecture; site heritage description alone cannot establish all regional military and labor relations.

mw-met-andes-1000.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Central and Southern Andes, 1000–1400 A.D.
mw-met-andes-1000.notes: Pre-Inca Andean regional states and material cultures; retrospective narrative and art-centered regional selection.

mw-met-seasia-1000.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Southeast Asia, 1000–1400 A.D.
mw-met-seasia-1000.notes: Southeast Asian state centers and temple traditions in 1000–1400; cultural survey does not exhaust port and household histories.

mw-cam-merchant-sultanates.title: Philippe Beaujard, Southeast Asia: Era of the Merchant Sultanates, in Worlds of the Indian Ocean, Cambridge
mw-cam-merchant-sultanates.notes: Indian Ocean and Southeast Asian mercantile sultanates, shifting trade and conversion; summary only, not the full monograph chapters.

mw-unesco-malay-annals.title: UNESCO Memory of the World, Sejarah Melayu (Malay Annals)
mw-unesco-malay-annals.notes: Malay Annals and Melaka tradition; late literary versions are not transparent eyewitness reporting of events around 1400.

mw-unesco-melaka.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Melaka and George Town, Historic Cities of the Straits of Malacca
mw-unesco-melaka.notes: Historical port and long-duration cosmopolitan exchange; colonial-era fabric also dominates inscription and cannot be retrojected indiscriminately before 1500.

mw-met-ming-1368.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Ming Dynasty (1368–1644)
mw-met-ming-1368.notes: Ming artistic and court contexts after Yuan, material culture; does not independently document detailed ship routes.

mw-smithsonian-zheng-he.title: Edward Dreyer, Zheng He: China and the Oceans in the Early Ming Dynasty, 1405–1433, Smithsonian Libraries bibliographic record
mw-smithsonian-zheng-he.notes: Identifies specialized study of Zheng He voyages and dates, but catalogue entry is not full book text; detailed voyages require direct documentary checking.

mw-met-interwoven-ocean.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Interwoven Globe: The Worldwide Textile Trade, 1500–1800
mw-met-interwoven-ocean.notes: Provides 1498 Portuguese entry into long-existing Indian Ocean trading world; most of this exhibition concerns AFTER 1500 and cannot describe all medieval networks.

mw-met-byzantium-330.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Byzantium (ca. 330–1453)
mw-met-byzantium-330.notes: Eastern Roman artistic and political traditions and conquest chronology; synthesis rather than primary eyewitness siege source.

mw-met-constantinople-1261.title: Annie Montgomery Labatt, Constantinople after 1261, Metropolitan Museum of Art
mw-met-constantinople-1261.notes: 1204 conquest, 1261 restoration, Palaiologan decline, plague and post-1453 city; urban and art focus, population estimates uncertain.

mw-met-ottomans-1600.title: Suzan Yalman, The Art of the Ottomans before 1600, Metropolitan Museum of Art
mw-met-ottomans-1600.notes: Formation of Ottoman dynasty, expanding territory, 1453 capture and rebuilding; later 16th-century events should not be projected back to 1500.

mw-met-balkans-1400.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Balkans, 1400–1600 A.D.
mw-met-balkans-1400.notes: Regional Ottoman and Balkan historical chronology; emphasis on artworks and dynasties, not complete social effects of frontiers.

mw-ox-hundred-years.title: Anne Curry, The Hundred Years War, Oxford academic reference article abstract
mw-ox-hundred-years.notes: Late medieval Anglo-French dynastic conflict and its chronology; abstract, not proof of all asserted local campaign impacts.

mw-met-florence-1400.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Florence and Central Italy, 1400–1600 A.D.
mw-met-florence-1400.notes: Florentine artistic and intellectual patronage; elite urban art history, not a claim that Renaissance changes reached all households equally.

mw-met-europe-print.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Central Europe, 1400–1600 A.D.
mw-met-europe-print.notes: Fifteenth-century Central Europe, printing and cultural shifts; does not license claiming European invention of printing globally.

mw-loc-columbus-taino.title: Library of Congress, Columbus and the Taíno
mw-loc-columbus-taino.notes: Caribbean peoples and Columbus landing in 1492; accompanying exhibit material frames early encounters and requires attention to colonial narration.

mw-loc-1492-expulsion.title: Library of Congress, 1492: An Ongoing Voyage, The Mediterranean
mw-loc-1492-expulsion.notes: 1492 Iberian, Mediterranean and religious context including persecution and expulsions; summary not exhaustive local legal or personal testimony.

gap-step-miller.title: Bryan K. Miller, Nomad Protagonists, in Xiongnu: The World’s First Nomadic Empire (Oxford, 2024)
gap-step-miller.notes: Specialist account of pastoral mobility, social institutions and Xiongnu power; only chapter abstract reviewed, not its unpublished full arguments.

gap-step-genomics.title: Lee et al., Genetic population structure of the Xiongnu Empire at imperial and local scales (Science Advances, 2023)
gap-step-genomics.notes: Ancient genomic diversity at sampled Xiongnu-period burials; sampled ancestry does not identify each person’s language, ethnic self-description or political loyalty.

gap-step-egiin.title: Joshua Wright, William Honeychurch, and Chunag Amartuvshin, The Xiongnu Settlements of Egiin Gol, Mongolia (Antiquity, 2009)
gap-step-egiin.notes: Survey supports Xiongnu-period settlements, mixed pastoral and cultivation practices; abstract only, and valley-specific evidence does not apply to all steppe peoples.

gap-step-world.title: The Cambridge World History, Introduction: The World from 1200 BCE to 900 CE
gap-step-world.notes: Broad scholarly synthesis of pastoral politics and varied forms of connection; not evidence for details of one household or precise political lineage.

gap-step-orkhon.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Orkhon Valley Cultural Landscape
gap-step-orkhon.notes: Archaeological remains from Turkic, Uighur and Mongol periods, including memorial monuments and urban centers; landscape inventory does not translate individual inscriptions.

gap-step-inscriptions.title: Turkic Atlas, Inscriptions: Orkhon-period monuments and texts
gap-step-inscriptions.notes: Chronology and descriptions of Old Turkic stelae including Kül Tegin and Tonyukuk; an online reference, not a critical edition of all readings.

gap-sog-letters.title: Nicholas Sims-Williams, Ancient Letters, in Smithsonian, The Sogdians
gap-sog-letters.notes: Curated document images and historical commentary including Miwnay, Shayn, Nanai-vandak and dating; letters are a small surviving sample.

gap-sog-translations.title: Nicholas Sims-Williams (translation), Daniel C. Waugh (introduction), The Sogdian Ancient Letters 1, 2, 3, and 5
gap-sog-translations.notes: Attributed translations of original Sogdian correspondence, source location and historical context; translations and restored readings are mediated scholarly interpretations.

gap-sog-iranica.title: Nicholas Sims-Williams, Ancient Letters, Encyclopaedia Iranica
gap-sog-iranica.notes: Specialist source description of letter discovery, form and addressees; document corpus is fragmentary and dates have been debated.

gap-sog-language.title: Nicholas Sims-Williams, Sogdian Language and Its Scripts, Smithsonian
gap-sog-language.notes: Written Sogdian, Aramaic-derived script conventions, and preservation geography; surviving documents are not a census of language speakers.

gap-sog-abroad.title: Smithsonian, The Sogdians Abroad
gap-sog-abroad.notes: Sogdian residents, merchants, interpreters and other work in China; mercantile emphasis cannot stand for all occupations.

gap-sog-murals.title: Julie Bellemare and Judith A. Lerner, Afrasiab Mural Paintings, Smithsonian
gap-sog-murals.notes: Mid-seventh-century court paintings and debated identifications of the central scene; images depict royal self-representation, not an unbiased event register.

gap-sog-religions.title: Smithsonian, Believers, Proselytizers, and Translators
gap-sog-religions.notes: Religious and textual plurality across Sogdian worlds; evidence for different dates and places cannot establish blanket tolerance.

gap-sog-intro.title: Smithsonian, Who Were the Sogdians?
gap-sog-intro.notes: Specialist exhibition orientation to Sogdian cities and varied occupations; synthetic exhibit rather than a complete primary archive.

gap-cah-unesco.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Cahokia Mounds State Historic Site
gap-cah-unesco.notes: Site, chronology, mounds, plazas and approximate peak population; official heritage estimates and classifications remain interpretive.

gap-cah-nps.title: US National Park Service, Cahokia Mounds State Historic Site: World Heritage Site
gap-cah-nps.notes: Site layout, residential areas and scale; visitor overview cannot identify undocumented leaders or individual labor obligations.

gap-cah-timber.title: Age and Origin of a Cahokian Wooden Monument at the Mitchell Site, Illinois (2025)
gap-cah-timber.notes: Dendrochronological and isotopic results for one marker post, dated c.1124 CE and sourced beyond local area; one object cannot map every exchange route.

gap-cah-hydro.title: Fecal Stanols Show Simultaneous Flooding and Seasonal Precipitation Change Correlate with Cahokia’s Population Decline (2019)
gap-cah-hydro.notes: Lake sediment proxies and possible climatic stress; associations are not a uniquely established cause of social change.

gap-cah-osage.title: Osage Nation, Osage Cultural History (Historic Preservation)
gap-cah-osage.notes: Osage accounts and analysis of cultural relationships with Mississippi Valley mound traditions; not a license to assign all Cahokia residents one modern identity.

gap-cah-name.title: National Geographic History, This American Indian Metropolis Was Mysteriously Abandoned (2021)
gap-cah-name.notes: Reports disputed interpretation and later origin of site name Cahokia; secondary journalistic synthesis, not original excavation.

gap-cha-nps-intro.title: US National Park Service, Chaco Culture National Historical Park: Puebloan History
gap-cha-nps-intro.notes: Regional chronology, major great houses, building features and descendant ties; interpretive visitor account.

gap-cha-nps-study.title: US National Park Service, Pueblo Period: The Archaeology of Chaco Canyon
gap-cha-nps-study.notes: Summarizes Steven Lekson’s edited scholarly synthesis (2006), archaeology of great houses, roads, exchange, and debates about site functions.

gap-cha-nps-oral.title: US National Park Service, Proto-Historic Period and Pueblo Oral Traditions
gap-cha-nps-oral.notes: Documents varied Pueblo and Navajo clan histories and cultural affiliations; no single contemporary community represents all ancestral experiences.

gap-cha-nps-faq.title: US National Park Service, Chaco Frequently Asked Questions
gap-cha-nps-faq.notes: Diet, water, beams, possible resource stresses and migration; explanations have different strengths of evidence.

gap-cha-nps-collection.title: US National Park Service, Chaco Archaeological Collection
gap-cha-nps-collection.notes: Primary site archive description of collected artifacts and timber sampling for dendrochronology; not a complete technical chronology.

gap-car-nmai.title: National Museum of the American Indian, Infinity of Nations: Mesoamerica/Caribbean
gap-car-nmai.notes: Pre-contact Caribbean diversity, Indigenous voyaging, political and artistic history; museum synthesis cannot specify every island’s practices.

gap-car-genetics.title: Fernandes et al., A Genetic History of the Pre-Contact Caribbean (Nature, 2021)
gap-car-genetics.notes: Ancient genome sampling, migration models and inter-island kinship; genomic ancestry is not a direct proxy for culture or a pre-contact census.

gap-car-caguana.title: Lidar Inspection for Indigenous Architecture at Caguana Ceremonial Complex, Borikén (Latin American Antiquity, 2021)
gap-car-caguana.notes: Archaeological mapping and chronology of ceremonial spaces at Caguana; ritual activities cannot be recovered exhaustively from ground features.

gap-car-nps.title: US National Park Service, Taíno Life, Belief, and Ceremony (Salt River Bay)
gap-car-nps.notes: Historical and archaeological account of caciques, gardens, zemís, bateyes and ceremonies; practices differ among island communities.

gap-car-met-zemi.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Taíno Zemí Figure (collection record)
gap-car-met-zemi.notes: Object dated 1200–1500 and cautious interpretation of ritual uses; context partly relies on later Spanish descriptions.

gap-car-met-collar.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Taíno Ceremonial Collar or Belt (collection record)
gap-car-met-collar.notes: Regalia and political symbolism circa 1000–1495, with specialist attributions; ritual meaning remains partly inferred.

gap-car-survival.title: Smithsonian, Caribbean Indigenous Resistance / Taíno Vive exhibition
gap-car-survival.notes: Indigenous Caribbean persistence after colonial violence; exhibition does not claim uniform continuity of every pre-contact practice.

gap-car-research.title: National Museum of the American Indian researchers, Bringing Taíno Peoples Back Into History
gap-car-research.notes: Research perspectives on survival, colonial records and oral histories; general article, not exhaustive documentary genealogy.

gap-dje-mcintosh.title: Roderick J. McIntosh and Susan Keech McIntosh, The Inland Niger Delta before the Empire of Mali: Evidence from Jenne-Jeno
gap-dje-mcintosh.notes: Original investigators’ published site chronology and early urban occupation; available extract, not full excavation dataset.

gap-dje-urban.title: Roderick J. McIntosh, Urbanization in the Middle Niger of Mali (Oxford Research Encyclopedia, 2021)
gap-dje-urban.notes: Regional satellite settlements and argument for possible heterarchy; interpretive synthesis available as abstract.

gap-dje-unesco.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Old Towns of Djenné
gap-dje-unesco.notes: Archaeological sites, material classes, chronologies and conservation setting; World Heritage statement combines earlier and later towns.

gap-dje-equality.title: Traditions of Equality: The Archaeology of Egalitarianism and Egalitarian Behavior in Sub-Saharan Africa (2025)
gap-dje-equality.notes: Recent scholarly discussion of heterarchical Djenné-Jeno and the limitations of excavated evidence; lack of elite remains does not logically establish equality.

gap-lake-research.title: Carlos Magnavita, Zakinet Dangbet, and Tchago Bouimon, The Lake Chad Region as a Crossroads (Afrique: Archéologie & Arts, 2019)
gap-lake-research.notes: Specialist research review of early Kanem–Borno documentary, oral and archaeological gaps, contested dating and possible intra-African links; proposed connections are research hypotheses.

gap-lake-trade.title: B. G. Martin, Kanem, Bornu and the Fazzān: Notes on the Political History of a Trade Route (Journal of African History)
gap-lake-trade.notes: History of Fezzan-Lake Chad caravan politics and 13th-century Kanem influence; available extract, not a study of every lakeshore household.

gap-ang-unesco.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Angkor
gap-ang-unesco.notes: Temples, hydraulic structures, region, chronology and modern communities; heritage record not a household census.

gap-ang-lidar.title: Damian H. Evans and colleagues, Uncovering Archaeological Landscapes at Angkor Using Lidar (PNAS, 2013)
gap-ang-lidar.notes: Open-access original field mapping of engineered landscapes and urban form; lidar maps shape but does not by itself date all features.

gap-ang-2016.title: Damian Evans, Airborne Laser Scanning as a Method for Exploring Long-Term Socio-Ecological Dynamics in Cambodia (J. Archaeol. Science, 2016)
gap-ang-2016.notes: Expanded lidar survey of Cambodian settlement landscapes; large-scale interpretation needs excavation and local chronology.

gap-ang-pop.title: Klassen and colleagues, Diachronic Modeling of the Population within the Medieval Greater Angkor Region Settlement Complex (Science Advances, 2021)
gap-ang-pop.notes: Modeled 700,000–900,000 residents at 13th-century apogee over a large region; not a census and depends on settlement-density assumptions.

gap-ang-inscriptions.title: Eileen Lustig and Terry Lustig, Losing Ground: Decline of Angkor’s Middle-Level Officials (J. Southeast Asian Studies, 2019)
gap-ang-inscriptions.notes: Translated Khmer inscription analysis of land transactions and temple endowments; available abstract, mainly legal/elite records.

gap-ang-occupation.title: Carter and colleagues, Temple Occupation and the Tempo of Collapse at Angkor Wat (PNAS, 2019)
gap-ang-occupation.notes: Excavation and radiocarbon evidence for transformation and later occupation, not total abandonment; dates apply to sampled local mound contexts.

gap-ang-crops.title: The Khmer Did Not Live by Rice Alone: Archaeobotanical Investigations at Angkor Wat and Ta Prohm (2020)
gap-ang-crops.notes: Site-specific archaebotanical evidence for multiple plant foods; food assemblages do not reconstruct every household diet.

gap-lake-dewiere.title: Rémi Dewière, The Kanem and Borno Sultanates (11th–19th Centuries), Oxford Research Encyclopedia of African History (2024)
gap-lake-dewiere.notes: Scholarly overview of Kanem and Borno dynastic chronology, Sayfawa relocation, Islamic elite institutions and later regional diplomacy; abstract only. Covers 11th–19th centuries and does not reconstruct ordinary households.

g2-gl-copper.title: Milwaukee Public Museum, Old Copper Culture
g2-gl-copper.notes: Copper-tool types, processing and early chronology in Great Lakes sites; object distribution does not identify the language or political identity of makers.

g2-gl-ont.title: Ontario Archaeological Society, Summary of Ontario Archaeology
g2-gl-ont.notes: Archaic and Woodland chronologies, shore changes, pottery, fishing and north-south subsistence differences; broad regional synthesis with locally variable dating.

g2-gl-maize.title: Gary W. Crawford, David G. Smith and Vandy E. Bowyer, Dating the Entry of Corn into the Lower Great Lakes Region (American Antiquity, 1997)
g2-gl-maize.notes: Five direct AMS dates at one Ontario site, calibrated circa 540–1030 CE; presence is not proof of region-wide dependence or identical farming practices.

g2-gl-hopewell.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Hopewell Ceremonial Earthworks
g2-gl-hopewell.notes: Chronology and characteristics of Ohio earthworks and distant raw materials; the modern Hopewell category is not an Indigenous self-designation.

g2-gl-nps.title: US National Park Service, Hopewell Earthworks
g2-gl-nps.notes: Archaeological labels, early excavations and colonial displacement affecting evidence; not a source for specific Great Lakes group identities.

g2-ne-nysm.title: New York State Museum, Mohawk Haudenosaunee Longhouse
g2-ne-nysm.notes: Household and clan description using archaeology, Haudenosaunee tradition and postcontact records; distinct evidence for different centuries.

g2-ne-jemison.title: Smithsonian Archives of American Art, Oral history interview with G. Peter Jemison (2021)
g2-ne-jemison.notes: Named Haudenosaunee account of the Peacemaker and Great Law; oral constitutional history is not by itself a precise archaeological founding date.

g2-ne-confed.title: Premodern Confederacies: Balancing Strategic Collective Action and Local Autonomy (Frontiers in Political Science, 2022)
g2-ne-confed.notes: Specialist comparison of Northern Iroquoian alliances and local autonomy; comparative interpretation, not authoritative replacement for nations’ own constitutions.

g2-ne-wendat.title: Archaeological History of the Wendat to AD 1651 (2015)
g2-ne-wendat.notes: Scholarly regional archaeology and cautions distinguishing Wendat, Iroquoian linguistic group, and Haudenosaunee politics; introductory public excerpt reviewed, not entire PDF.

g2-nw-kwaxistalla.title: Kwakwaka’wakw Clam Gardens: Motive and Practice among an Indigenous Community (Human Ecology, 2015)
g2-nw-kwaxistalla.notes: Research includes Indigenous knowledge of Kwaxistalla Adam Dick about tending clam beds; specific regional practices must not be imposed unchanged coast-wide.

g2-nw-quadra.title: Ancestral Sea Gardens Supported Human Settlements for at Least 3,800 Years (Frontiers in Earth Science, 2022)
g2-nw-quadra.notes: Archaeology and community research in bays of northern Quadra Island; dated local sequence, not universal age for every clam garden.

g2-nw-dating.title: Between a Rock and a Soft Place: Optical Ages of Ancient Clam Gardens (PLOS ONE, 2017)
g2-nw-dating.notes: Optical dating constraints and uncertainties of construction and sediment burial; sample dates need archaeological context.

g2-nw-traps.title: Fish Traps as Evidence of Changing Social Cooperation and Investment on the Pacific Northwest Coast (Journal of Anthropological Archaeology, 2026)
g2-nw-traps.notes: Compilation of 511 radiocarbon dates from over 200 traps; correlations with settlement do not identify organizers or exact rights.

g2-nw-synthesis.title: Indigenous Marine Resource Management on the Northwest Coast of North America (Ecological Processes, 2013)
g2-nw-synthesis.notes: Research synthesis on harvesting, weirs, shellfish and management; examples vary across community, habitat, and period.

g2-nw-burke.title: Burke Museum, Traditional Home Engineering (educator resource, 2020)
g2-nw-burke.notes: Distinguishes coastal cedar plank houses from interior tule-mat house engineering; short public excerpt reviewed, not a dated excavation.

g2-nub-ruffini-intro.title: Giovanni R. Ruffini, Qasr Ibrim and Christian Nubia, Medieval Nubia: A Social and Economic History (Oxford, 2012)
g2-nub-ruffini-intro.notes: Site, documentary archives and regional historical frame; chapter abstract only, so no undocumented scene details.

g2-nub-ruffini-land.title: Giovanni R. Ruffini, Qasr Ibrim’s Land Sales (Oxford, 2012)
