g2-nub-ruffini-land.notes: Old Nubian sales including third-party transfers and earlier editions of Gerald Browne; abstract does not establish broad population rates.

g2-nub-ruffini-mash.title: Giovanni R. Ruffini, Mashshouda and Archive 3 (Oxford, 2012)
g2-nub-ruffini-mash.notes: Prosopographical reinterpretation of a named Qasr Ibrim archive; Mashshouda’s title remains uncertain.

g2-nub-ruffini-conc.title: Giovanni R. Ruffini, Conclusion: Medieval Nubian Society and Gender (Oxford, 2012)
g2-nub-ruffini-conc.notes: Highlights women’s land ownership, royal succession and the limits of archive extrapolation; publicly available abstract rather than full chapter.

g2-nub-ruffini-ceremony.title: Giovanni R. Ruffini, Nubian Land Sales as Ceremony (Oxford, 2012)
g2-nub-ruffini-ceremony.notes: Interpretation of witnesses and food/drink in legal transactions; ceremonial meaning is a scholarly hypothesis.

g2-nub-ruffini-money.title: Giovanni R. Ruffini, Money, Rent, Taxes, and Investment (Oxford, 2012)
g2-nub-ruffini-money.notes: Reconstruction of monetary ratios and rents from specific archives; not a full Nubian economic census.

g2-nub-khan.title: Geoffrey Khan, Arabic Documents from Medieval Nubia (Open Book Publishers, 2024)
g2-nub-khan.notes: Edition and translations of Qasr Ibrim Arabic corpus; manuscripts preserve formal legal and administrative perspectives rather than unconstrained inner voices.

g2-nub-khan-legal.title: Geoffrey Khan, Legal Documents, Arabic Documents from Medieval Nubia (2024)
g2-nub-khan-legal.notes: Identifies numbered leases, land transactions, marriage, divorce and judges’ correspondence; legal forms must be read critically.

g2-nub-khan-eparchs.title: Geoffrey Khan, Correspondence with Eparchs, Arabic Documents from Medieval Nubia (2024)
g2-nub-khan-eparchs.notes: Letters between Muslim merchants and Nubian officials and exchange including enslaved people; archive is selective.

g2-nub-maryam50.title: Princeton Geniza Project, Qasr Ibrim document 50, translation by Geoffrey Khan
g2-nub-maryam50.notes: A dated formal divorce acknowledgement concerning Maryam; the legal document is not her firsthand interior testimony.

g2-nub-maryam53.title: Princeton Geniza Project, Qasr Ibrim document 53, edited and translated by Geoffrey Khan
g2-nub-maryam53.notes: Letter concerning Maryam and competing marital claims; reflects a judicial perspective and missing context.

g2-sw-unesco.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani and Songo Mnara
g2-sw-unesco.notes: Site locations, date ranges, mosques, coral houses and maritime connections; heritage description not a census of household activity.

g2-sw-york.title: University of York, Stephanie Wynne-Jones research profile and Songo Mnara project
g2-sw-york.notes: Methods and site focus of household and open-space research; institutional summary, not full specialist dataset.

g2-sw-walshaw.title: Sarah Walshaw, Cooking and Crafting at Songo Mnara: Macrobotanical Remains (2015)
g2-sw-walshaw.notes: Published abstract on plant remains from stone and earthen buildings; abstract excerpt reviewed, not detailed sample distributions.

g2-sw-public.title: Jeffrey Fleisher and Federica Sulas, Deciphering Public Spaces at Songo Mnara (Journal of Archaeological Science, 2015)
g2-sw-public.notes: Spatial method synthesis and conclusions about open spaces; abstract only, no claim to precise identities.

g2-sw-coins.title: John Perkins, Jeffrey Fleisher and Stephanie Wynne-Jones, A Deposit of Kilwa-Type Coins from Songo Mnara (Azania, 2014)
g2-sw-coins.notes: Well-contextualized coin deposit from a stonehouse foundation; interpretation as investing value in place is tentative.

g2-bag-unesco.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Bagan
g2-bag-unesco.notes: 11th–13th-century monument landscape, endowment politics, Ayeyarwady, continuing communities and practices; not household legal archive.

g2-bag-myazedi.title: UNESCO Memory of the World, Myazedi Quadrilingual Stone Inscription
g2-bag-myazedi.notes: Four script/language faces, Bagan setting, dating to 1113; monument’s multilingual text is not a census.

g2-bag-field.title: IRAW@Bagan 2018 field season report: residential patterning, agricultural practices and water management
g2-bag-field.notes: Research report discusses inscriptions and nonmonumental landscapes; web excerpt reviewed, and later chronicles distinguished from contemporary evidence.

g2-bag-architecture.title: Religious Symbols as Decorations on the Sikhara of Ancient Monuments in the Late Bagan Period (Bagan and the World, 2018)
g2-bag-architecture.notes: 13th-century monuments, decorative styles and inscription dating; chapter abstract only.

g2-java-boro.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Borobudur Temple Compounds
g2-java-boro.notes: Buddhist architecture, 8th–9th-century chronology, Sailendra connections and reliefs; architecture cannot reconstruct all labor or village life.

g2-java-pram.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Prambanan Temple Compounds
g2-java-pram.notes: Hindu and Buddhist temple complexes and dates in central Java; religious labels do not map every household.

g2-java-sima.title: Miho Yamasaki, The Reign and the Royal Authority in King Balitung’s Period: Old Javanese Inscriptions (2015)
g2-java-sima.notes: Named sima land/tax grants connecting kings, officials and religious foundations; source is abstract for article.

g2-java-maj.title: UNESCO Tentative List, Trowulan: Former Capital City of Majapahit Kingdom (Indonesian nomination)
g2-java-maj.notes: Archaeological objects and settlement traces at Trowulan; state-party heritage nomination includes hypotheses and advocacy claims.

g2-java-poem.title: The Galactic Polity in Southeast Asia, with discussion of fourteenth-century Majapahit and Nagarakretagama (HAU, 2013)
g2-java-poem.notes: Interpretive analysis of Prapanca’s court poem and uneven political reach; abstract/excerpt not evidence of direct rule over listed areas.

g2-tur-berlin.title: Simone-Christiane Raschmann, The Berlin Turfan Collection (Berlin State Library)
g2-tur-berlin.notes: Scripts, languages, texts, collecting history and problems of cyclical dates; curator synthesis not a translation of an individual contract.

g2-tur-bbaw.title: Berlin-Brandenburg Academy, Turfanforschung / Turfan Studies
g2-tur-bbaw.notes: Current edition and cataloguing of religious, commercial, monastic and letter texts in numerous languages; collection summary.

g2-tur-books.title: University of Hamburg, Reconstructing Old Uyghur Book Forms (2023–25)
g2-tur-books.notes: Fragment-based reconstruction and book forms; not a survey of all oasis households.

g2-tur-script.title: Staatsbibliothek zu Berlin, Berlin Turfan Collection: secular and religious manuscripts
g2-tur-script.notes: Old Uyghur texts, Sogdian-derived script, economic fragments and 12-year animal calendar dating; fragmentary records limit precision.

g2-tur-museum.title: Museum für Asiatische Kunst, The Turfan Collection and Expeditions
g2-tur-museum.notes: 1902–1914 collecting history, archival records and provenance; modern institutional perspective, not medieval political history.

g2-tur-forms.title: Berlin-Brandenburg Academy, Turfan Studies manuscript catalogues
g2-tur-forms.notes: Editing of Uyghur economic texts, manuscripts, block prints and multilingual material; a cataloguing overview.

g3-mv-ua.title: University of Alabama Museums, Moundville Archaeological Park, Ancient Site
g3-mv-ua.notes: Black Warrior setting, phased occupancy, plaza, palisade, mounds, ceremonial transformation; museum synthesis of archaeological research.

g3-mv-blitz.title: John H. Blitz, Moundville in the Mississippian World, Oxford Handbook of North American Archaeology (2012)
g3-mv-blitz.notes: Specialist four-phase occupation chronology and social-memory interpretation; only abstract publicly reviewed.

g3-mv-ency.title: Vernon James Knight and Encyclopedia of Alabama, Moundville Archaeological Park
g3-mv-ency.notes: Settlement, maize, occupations, construction, burials and shifting population; estimates and elite interpretations are reconstructive.

g3-mv-tribal.title: Moundville Archaeological Park, Self Guided Tour (2026), prepared with descendant Tribal communities
g3-mv-tribal.notes: Names living Tribal Nations, distinguishes archaeological label from community identity, describes material culture and changing burial role; official descendant-collaborative interpretation, not exact lineage census.

g3-mv-exhibit.title: Moundville Archaeological Park, The Home of Our Ancestors exhibit co-curated by Jake Tiger (2026)
g3-mv-exhibit.notes: Current Seminole co-curation and continuities of craft and culture; not independent proof of individual ancient genealogies.

g3-pl-npspeople.title: National Park Service, Knife River People
g3-pl-npspeople.notes: Upper Missouri riverine farming, bison hunting, earthlodges and oral accounts; many described villages are post-1500, so avoid unqualified projection.

g3-pl-npsplaces.title: National Park Service, Places at Knife River Indian Villages
g3-pl-npsplaces.notes: Geography, Hidatsa farm labor, earthlodge village traces and historic livelihoods; contact-era evidence cannot establish all prehistoric practices.

g3-pl-npsarticle.title: National Park Service, Knife River Indian Villages National Historic Site
g3-pl-npsarticle.notes: Village chronology and later Mandan/Hidatsa/Arikara history, including main Knife River site dates after 1525; careful pre-1500 scope required.

g3-pl-middle.title: US National Park Service National Register, Bison Kill Sites in South Dakota thematic context, Middle Missouri archaeology
g3-pl-middle.notes: Archaeological context for Middle Missouri houses, village layout, mixed horticulture and hunting from AD 900 onward; regional synthesis and interpretive assignments.

g3-pl-education.title: National Park Service, Knife River: Early Village Life on the Plains
g3-pl-education.notes: Earthlodge engineering and documented Mandan/Hidatsa/Arikara households, later-era descriptions that must not be assumed unchanged for year 1000.

g3-arctic-sirm.title: Parks Canada, Sirmilik National Park: History
g3-arctic-sirm.notes: Eastern Arctic Dorset and Thule occupation, house construction, hunting and mobility; Indigenous descent and uncertainty of interactions.

g3-arctic-ivv.title: Parks Canada, Ivvavik National Park: Culture and history
g3-arctic-ivv.notes: Beaufort Sea settlement and subsequent regional adaptation, including thirteenth-century developments; park-region specificity.

g3-arctic-tuktut.title: Parks Canada, Tuktut Nogait: Culture and history
g3-arctic-tuktut.notes: Regional archaeological site distribution and c. 1200–1500 occupation, not a general chronology for entire Arctic.

g3-arctic-review.title: Arctic Archaeology and Climate Change, Annual Review of Anthropology (2019)
g3-arctic-review.notes: Scholarly review of dispersal, subsistence variability, whales, exchange and climate responses; long-term synthesis with regional uncertainty.

g3-arctic-qutt.title: Parks Canada, Quttinirpaaq Management Plan: Arctic archaeological sequence
g3-arctic-qutt.notes: High Arctic archaeological evidence and Inuit heritage technologies, site variation and preservation.

g3-et-unesco.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Rock-Hewn Churches, Lalibela
g3-et-unesco.notes: Architecture, sacred geography, related town remains and conservation; royal foundation narrative is heritage tradition not independent construction dating.

g3-et-rock.title: The rock-cut churches of Lalibela and cave church of Washa Mikael, Antiquity 95 (2021)
g3-et-rock.notes: Specialist archaeological evidence of earlier troglodytic cultures and stages of Christianization; public abstract, not full field data.

g3-et-lund.title: Lund University, The Church of Yimrhane Kristos: An Archaeological Investigation (2018)
g3-et-lund.notes: Archaeometry, wood analysis, inscriptions and qualified use of hagiographic evidence; public research summary.

g3-et-settlement.title: Settlement archaeology and oral history in Lasta, Ethiopia (2009)
g3-et-settlement.notes: Lalibela settlement context beyond churches and oral-history approaches; public abstract only.

g3-et-land.title: Administrative and military impediments of medieval Ethiopian economy, Cogent Arts & Humanities (2023)
g3-et-land.notes: Discussion of gwelt, revenue claims and medieval Ethiopian officials; predominantly later medieval systems, avoid back-projection.

g3-geniza-pgp.title: Princeton Geniza Project, Digital Corpus and introduction
g3-geniza-pgp.notes: Institutional history, letters, contracts, catalog and translations; corpus reflects documented Jewish communities, not population-wide sample.

g3-geniza-court.title: Princeton Geniza Project, Legal document T-S 12.558
g3-geniza-court.notes: Cairo 1180s court notebook and half-house arrangement involving Sitt al-Fakhr; editorial description based on Goitein and Amir Ashur.

g3-geniza-letter.title: Princeton Geniza Project, Letter T-S 10J15.9, including edited translation
g3-geniza-letter.notes: Woman to absent husband, illness, family dispute, possible divorce; fragmentary text and contested reconstructions.

g3-geniza-goldberg.title: Jessica L. Goldberg, The use and abuse of commercial letters from the Cairo Geniza, Journal of Medieval History (2012)
g3-geniza-goldberg.notes: Commercial letter genres, business networks and why requests are not neutral transaction reports.

g3-geniza-krak.title: Eve Krakowski, Coming of Age in Medieval Egypt, Princeton University Press (2018)
g3-geniza-krak.notes: Study of Fatimid and Ayyubid Jewish girls, wealth, legal practice and household diversity; book description reviewed, not full text.

g3-geniza-rustow.title: Princeton University, Marina Rustow and the Cairo Geniza: Fragile Fragments (2019)
g3-geniza-rustow.notes: Geniza discovery, storage and dispersion, documents and public-administration research; institutional reporting on scholarly work.

g3-geniza-women.title: Posen Library, Letter to Her Sister, early twelfth century
g3-geniza-women.notes: Describes female author/scribe, family, guardianship and inheritance; publicly reviewed editorial summary rather than full restricted text.

g3-dvar-oxford.title: Wesley Clarke and Matthew Gallon, Early States in Thailand: Dvaravati, Oxford Handbook of Early Southeast Asia (2022)
g3-dvar-oxford.notes: Sixth–eleventh-century archaeology, uncertain polity form, poorly documented domestic sites, limitations of monument-centered research; abstract only.

g3-dvar-met.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Lost Kingdoms exhibition: Dvaravati Buddhist art (2014)
g3-dvar-met.notes: Sculpture, monumental images, wheels and narrative reliefs; museum art history does not demonstrate state boundaries.

g3-dvar-chron.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Southeast Asia 500–1000 CE Chronology
g3-dvar-chron.notes: Regional chronology, Dvaravati, Mon and trade connections; overview with simplifications about statehood.

g3-dvar-inscr.title: East and West: New Inscriptions from Funan, Zhenla and Dvaravati, BEFEO (2021)
g3-dvar-inscr.notes: New Nakhon Pathom Sanskrit epigraphy and paleographic date uncertainty; local elite claims not polity-wide map.

g3-dvar-trade.title: The International Trade in Dvaravati Period: Archaeology of Nakhon Pathom, Silpakorn University Journal (2013)
g3-dvar-trade.notes: Excavated Tang pottery and nonlocal beads, contacts and trade; site-specific interpretation from abstract.

g3-dvar-smith.title: Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art, Dvaravati period stucco objects
g3-dvar-smith.notes: Khu Bua and related sculpture chronology and provenance; art objects cannot establish household demographics.

g3-cham-unesco.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, My Son Sanctuary
g3-cham-unesco.notes: Thu Bon valley landscape, My Son temple forms and sanctuary chronology; heritage account tends to present a singular Cham kingdom.

g3-cham-oxford.title: William A. Southworth, Champa, Oxford Handbook of Early Southeast Asia (2022)
g3-cham-oxford.notes: Tra Kieu, Go Cam, Han China, Sanskrit and Cham inscriptions, poor domestic ceramic dating; specialist abstract only.

g3-cham-dissert.title: My Ket Chau, Communities and Cultural Exchanges of Champa: Art of the Chams in Central and Southern Vietnam, UCLA (2020)
g3-cham-dissert.notes: Networked ritual arts, four pedestal-shrines, mixed interpretations, maritime links; dissertation abstract publicly reviewed.

g3-cham-polity.title: Mai Bui Dieu Linh, Religious Identity and Contemporary Ritual Practices of the Cham Ahier in Vietnam, Extreme-Orient Extreme-Occident 45 (2022; online 2025)
g3-cham-polity.notes: The article discusses river-valley versus five-principality models of Champa and cites the competing argument from fifteenth-century epigraphy for a more extensive kingdom; this is a review of the debate in a study primarily of present-day Cham Ahier practice.

g3-dun-history.title: International Dunhuang Programme, History of the IDP and Cave 17
g3-dun-history.notes: Sealing, discovery, dispersion of Cave 17 materials; institutional history of collections.

g3-dun-languages.title: International Dunhuang Programme, What Was Stored in Cave 17?
g3-dun-languages.notes: Languages, religious texts, documents, Old Tibetan Annals and cave contents; collection-level profile.

g3-dun-timeline.title: International Dunhuang Programme, A Timeline of Dunhuang
g3-dun-timeline.notes: Tibetan rule approximately 781–848 and local Guiyijun regime; overview chronology.

g3-dun-work.title: International Dunhuang Programme, Dunhuang at Work
g3-dun-work.notes: Census, irrigation, taxes, local administration and diplomatic responsibilities under Guiyijun; general archive synthesis.

g3-dun-scribes.title: International Dunhuang Programme, Scribes at Dunhuang: Pens, Paper and Punishments (2025)
g3-dun-scribes.notes: Named IOL Tib J 1359 scribal-paper register and IOL Tib J 1274 Ser Dzinkheng wrapper; records threats, not measured enforcement.

g3-dun-circular.title: International Dunhuang Programme, Entertainment and Social Life
g3-dun-circular.notes: 886 circular for meeting, fines, signatures and other local associations; translated summary of original document.

g3-dun-guangde.title: International Dunhuang Programme, Daily Life Collection Items, contract of 916
g3-dun-guangde.notes: Contract recording transfer of seven-year-old Guangde by mother A Wu, coercion and reused scroll; cannot establish the child’s later fate.

g3-dun-taenzer.title: Gertraud Taenzer, The Dunhuang Region during Tibetan Rule (787–848): A Study of Secular Manuscripts, Harrassowitz (2012)
g3-dun-taenzer.notes: Chinese and Tibetan tax records, land, contracts and mixed administrative practice; part of scholarly book accessible in JSTOR text preview.

g4-de-shimada.title: Akira Shimada, Royal and Non-Royal Buddhist Patronage in the Early Deccan (2018)
g4-de-shimada.notes: Peer-reviewed abstract: first century BCE to third century CE cave patronage, contrast between imperial gifts and collective local support; only abstract consulted.

g4-de-singh.title: Upinder Singh, Yavanas in Early Indian Inscriptions, in Classical Art and Ancient India
g4-de-singh.notes: Research excerpt: named Yavana donors at Karle and Nasik, ambiguous identity terms and dated inscriptions. Search-extracted PDF passages, not an independent edition of inscriptions.

g4-de-endow.title: Religious Endowments in Ancient India and the Institutionalization of Brahmin Caste Status (American Journal of Legal History, 2023)
g4-de-endow.notes: Full public scholarly page details early Kshaharata grants at Karla and Nasik, including village and field endowments; grant claims should not be mistaken for a tenant census.

g4-de-dehejia.title: Vidya Dehejia, Early Buddhist Rock Temples: chronology and inscriptions (1972)
g4-de-dehejia.notes: Search excerpt of scholarly study: site chronology, merchant Bhutapala and other Karle inscriptional patrons, difficulties of paleographic dating.

g4-de-smarthistory.title: Smarthistory, A Brief History of the Art of South Asia: Prehistory to c. 500 CE
g4-de-smarthistory.notes: Public art-history synthesis on rock-cut cave architecture, Karle wooden elements and regional religious construction.

g4-de-patronage.title: Buddhist Patronage, Brill scholarly chapter
g4-de-patronage.notes: Search excerpt comparing collective caitya donors and large royal vihara endowments; no complete scholarly PDF analysis claimed.

g4-ch-utt.title: INFLIBNET, The Cholas: Uttaramerur inscriptions and village committees
g4-ch-utt.notes: Indian academic open lesson describing 919 and 921 inscriptions, qualification and lot-drawing, committee roles and relations to royal officials; one village not representative of all.

g4-ch-admin.title: INFLIBNET e-PG Pathshala, Cholas: Provincial and Local Administration
g4-ch-admin.notes: Search excerpt differentiates ur, sabha, brahmadeya and vellanvagai settlements and social hierarchy; academic secondary synthesis.

g4-ch-thapar.title: Romila Thapar, History of Early India: From the Origins to AD 1300 (Uttaramerur passage)
g4-ch-thapar.notes: Search-extracted historical passage quotes inscription and cites Archaeological Survey of India 1904-05 report, noting rule revision and disputes.

g4-ch-karashima.title: Noboru Karashima, A Concise History of South India: Issues and Interpretations (2014)
g4-ch-karashima.notes: Search-extracted chapter compares ur and brahmadeya sabha, landholding and the limitations of generalized local-government narratives.

g4-ch-asi.title: Archaeological Survey of India, Great Living Chola Temples
g4-ch-asi.notes: Government archaeological overview: temples, Chola royal patrons and inscriptions recording donations, arrangements and aspects of society.

g4-pa-museum.title: National Museum New Delhi, Nalanda copper plate grant of Devapala
g4-pa-museum.notes: Museum object record, accession 47.51, identifies Devapala grant of five villages requested by Balaputradeva for monastic maintenance and copying texts.

g4-pa-edition.title: Hirananda Shastri, Nalanda and Its Epigraphic Material: Devapala copper plate
g4-pa-edition.notes: Search excerpt of published epigraphic translation names five donated villages and terms of support; original edition and editorial interpretation must be distinguished.

g4-pa-digital.title: Pramana, Nalanda copper-plate of Devapala, edition of Shastri (1924)
g4-pa-digital.notes: Digital transcription/index of the Sanskrit royal grant and scholarly edition; differing regnal-year descriptions in reference literature should not be silently reconciled.

g4-pa-nalanda.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Archaeological Site of Nalanda Mahavihara
g4-pa-nalanda.notes: Excavated monastery and shrine sequence, centuries of rebuilding, intellectual connections; UNESCO institutional synthesis is not a census of students.

g4-pa-somapura.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Ruins of the Buddhist Vihara at Paharpur
g4-pa-somapura.notes: Somapura/Paharpur at Naogaon in modern Bangladesh, association with Pala patronage, archaeological structure and artistic influence.

g4-gb-nevada.title: Nevada State Historic Preservation Office, People of the Humboldt
g4-gb-nevada.notes: State archaeological/heritage synthesis: terminal basin wetlands, Lovelock site, nets, birds, fish and Northern Paiute histories; not an individual site report for all periods.

g4-gb-blm.title: Bureau of Land Management, Lovelock Cave Historic Site
g4-gb-blm.notes: Federal site record for tule duck decoys, thousands of recovered objects, colonial-era collecting and repatriation; object ages vary.

g4-gb-nps.title: National Park Service, Fremont Culture, Great Basin National Park
g4-gb-nps.notes: Fremont archaeological label, mixed farming and foraging, culture change and differing Numic interpretations; do not equate labels with peoples.

g4-gb-museum.title: Natural History Museum of Utah, Fremont Archaeology
g4-gb-museum.notes: Museum archaeology: Noel Morss archaeological label and c. 300-1300 CE agriculture, settlement, granaries, rock art and variability.

g4-gb-dinosaur.title: National Park Service, Fremont Culture, Dinosaur National Monument
g4-gb-dinosaur.notes: Regional seasonal occupations, shelters, stored food, wild resources and cultivation; monument-specific dating not automatically Great Basin-wide.

g4-so-nps.title: National Park Service, The Ancestral Sonoran Desert People, Casa Grande
g4-so-nps.notes: Regional site interpretation, irrigation, material archaeology, naming conventions and the shift toward platform mounds; no proof of centralized canal authority.

g4-so-canal.title: National Park Service, Hohokam Culture
g4-so-canal.notes: Government archaeological synthesis on canal networks, fields, settlement and platform mounds; some population estimates are approximate.

g4-so-house.title: National Park Service, The Casa Grande and ancestral Sonoran Desert building
g4-so-house.notes: Public site page identifies caliche construction, c.1350 Great House and uncertainty concerning its purpose.

g4-so-tribal.title: Salt River Pima-Maricopa Indian Community, Onk Akimel Oodham and Huhugam
g4-so-tribal.notes: Direct community account of river peoples, ancestral relationships and distinction between Oodham huhugam and archaeology-specific hohokam.

g4-so-wayside.title: National Park Service, Ball Games, Platform Mounds, and Great Houses
g4-so-wayside.notes: NPS site interpretation of successive public structures and changed gathering centers; site-specific temporal relationship.

g4-so-research.title: National Park Service, A New Way of Documenting and Imaging Cultural Resources: Casa Grande
g4-so-research.notes: Recent survey and documentation of Casa Grande architecture, uncertainty and disturbance; built-date estimates vary across publications.

g4-pu-nps.title: National Park Service, People of Mesa Verde
g4-pu-nps.notes: Site interpretation foregrounding descendant Pueblo nations, movement and multiple sources of evidence, not an exhaustive chronology for all Pueblo peoples.

g4-pu-crow.title: Crow Canyon Archaeological Center, Pueblo III overview (1150-1300 CE)
g4-pu-crow.notes: Archaeological center account of aggregation into larger Mesa Verde region settlements c.1250.

g4-pu-post.title: Crow Canyon Archaeological Center, Post-Pueblo Period
g4-pu-post.notes: Archaeological synthesis linking migration to continued Pueblo communities in New Mexico and Arizona.

g4-pu-kuck.title: Kristin A. Kuckelman, Depopulation of Sand Canyon Pueblo, American Antiquity 75 (2010)
g4-pu-kuck.notes: Peer-reviewed abstract: local excavation indicates drought-related food stress and a violent attack at Sand Canyon; not a model for every migration.

g4-pu-glow.title: Donna M. Glowacki, Living and Leaving: A Social History of Regional Depopulation in Thirteenth-Century Mesa Verde (2015)
g4-pu-glow.notes: Specialist monograph description and overview of varied social, political, climatic and migration factors; full text not reviewed.

g4-pu-tree.title: Mesa Verde Settlement History and Relocation, Kiva 72 (2007)
g4-pu-tree.notes: Peer-reviewed abstract on tree-ring precipitation sequences and pottery-based regional contacts; interpretation limited by proxies.

g4-si-kci.title: On the Record Date of Silla Village Register, Korean Citation Index article (2017)
g4-si-kci.notes: Academic abstract summarizes four village documents in Shosoin, crops, animals, and a paleographic argument for 695 CE; date is disputed.

g4-si-study.title: Silla Village Register, Gyeongju Silla Studies web library research summary
g4-si-study.notes: Korean-language site notes document discovery as reused Buddhist manuscript binding and date arguments including 695, 755, and 815 CE.

g4-si-age.title: Park Namsoo, Age Classifications in the Silla Village Registers (2022)
g4-si-age.notes: Scholarly abstract on age classification and village society; data interpretation and dates are debated.

g4-si-household.title: Lee Hyun-ju, Family and Household Registers in Silla (2026)
g4-si-household.notes: Academic abstract distinguishes kinship families from administrative households used for taxation; not a full translation of record.

g4-si-plants.title: Journal of Korean Art and Archaeology, Archaeobotanical review of Korean plant materials
g4-si-plants.notes: Search excerpt compares tree species in Silla registers with sparse physical plant remains and uncertain identifications.

g4-si-history.title: History of Silla, Gyeongsangbuk-do Research Institution English summary
g4-si-history.notes: Official English specialist historical survey mentions registration, crops, and early Korean state context; searched excerpt only.

g4-ba-oxford.title: Oxford Invisible East, Bactrian Documents: inventory from northern Afghanistan
g4-ba-oxford.notes: Detailed document catalogue gives types, sites, Bactrian Era dates and reconstructed CE chronology, including document U vineyard lease.

g4-ba-sims.title: University of Toronto Iranian Studies, Nicholas Sims-Williams, Bactrian Documents and Archives (2024)
g4-ba-sims.notes: Scholar webinar abstract describes Bactrian-language letters, leases, contracts, language and insecure findspots; no direct archaeological provenience claimed.

g4-ba-slave.title: Slavery Represented in Bactrian Documents, Slavery and Abolition (2023)
g4-ba-slave.notes: Peer-reviewed public article discusses Rob document U vineyard lease and enslaved persons in Bactrian contracts; legal terms interpreted by modern editor.

g4-ba-chron.title: Nicholas Sims-Williams and Francois de Blois, Studies in the Chronology of the Bactrian Documents from Northern Afghanistan (2018)
g4-ba-chron.notes: Scholarly book description: 150+ documents and disputed Bactrian Era conversion; full monograph not reviewed.

g5-ta-champa.title: R. Champakalakshmi, Sangam Literature as Evidence on India’s Trade: Problems of Methodology and Interpretation (UNESCO Silk Roads paper)
g5-ta-champa.notes: Public PDF text extraction of a scholarly methodological paper. Poems are conventional literary compositions compiled later; historical trade claims are indirect and dates debated. The legacy URL currently redirects in some clients.

g5-ta-escholar.title: Canons, Conventions and Creativity: Defining Literary Tradition in Premodern Tamil South India (UC eScholarship)
g5-ta-escholar.notes: University thesis/article search excerpt on akam, puram, tinai and uncertain Sangam composition dates; full site did not load during review.

g5-ta-keeladi.title: Excavations at Keeladi, Sivaganga District, Tamil Nadu: published archaeological report
g5-ta-keeladi.notes: Report excerpt describes inscribed Tamil-Brahmi pottery and archaeological contexts; attribution of individual names and dates is interpretive. Not a direct measure of literacy rates.

g5-ta-tamili.title: Tamili Inscribed Potsherds: An Introduction (Tamil digital library)
g5-ta-tamili.notes: Specialist catalogue search excerpt of inscriptions across sites; counts depend on survey and excavation and should not imply population-wide literacy.

g5-gt-christie.title: Jan Wisseman Christie, The Medieval Tamil-language Inscriptions in Southeast Asia and China, Journal of Southeast Asian Studies 29(2) (1998)
g5-gt-christie.notes: Scholarly article page with detailed references and excerpts on guild inscriptions; some full-text access restricted.

g5-gt-mckinnon.title: E. Edwards McKinnon, Continuity and Change in South Indian Involvement in Northern Sumatra (Cambridge/ISEAS)
g5-gt-mckinnon.notes: Public chapter summary identifies the 1088 CE Lobu Tua Tamil guild text and locally sourced benzoin and camphor; not the full excavation volume.

g5-gt-barus.title: An Indian Ocean Port: Sources for the Earlier History of Barus, Archipel (1989)
g5-gt-barus.notes: Public historical article discusses Barus and the 1088 guild inscription through earlier readings; consult Subbarayalu’s edited text for exact disputed wording.

g5-gt-subbarayalu.title: Y. Subbarayalu, The Tamil Merchant-Guild Inscription at Barus: A Rediscovery (1998), reviewed in Bulletin critique des Annales islamologiques
g5-gt-subbarayalu.notes: Public review of the edited inscription and Lobu Tua excavation reports, including camphor/benzoin materials and 1088 dating; not a direct manuscript transcript.

g5-ca-nps.title: National Park Service, Chumash Midden: maritime technology and bead exchange
g5-ca-nps.notes: Government site interpretation on tomol plank canoes, shell beads and island-mainland exchange; present-day canoe revitalization documented. Site synthesis, not comprehensive precontact ethnography.

g5-ca-gamble.title: Lynn H. Gamble, The Origin and Use of Shell Bead Money in California, Journal of Anthropological Archaeology (2020)
g5-ca-gamble.notes: Peer-reviewed abstract argues shell bead currency may date earlier than older 800-year proposal. Distinguishes exchange media from all beads; full paid paper not reviewed.

g5-ca-fire.title: US Forest Service, Tribal Cultural Resources and Cultural Use of Fire
g5-ca-fire.notes: Federal synthesis of Indigenous land-management uses of fire for acorns, baskets, habitat and safety. Practices varied by tribe, place and period.

g5-ca-oak.title: US Forest Service, Fire History of California Oak Woodlands (Studies in Avian Biology)
g5-ca-oak.notes: Research excerpt on practices under oaks and fire effects; historical/ethnographic interpretation is not a site-specific archaeological date.

g5-pl-nmai.title: Smithsonian National Museum of the American Indian, Columbia River/Plateau Region (Native Knowledge 360)
g5-pl-nmai.notes: Museum educational resource with Indigenous interview and continuing salmon practices. Modern photos and testimony are not a timestamp for a medieval fishery.

g5-pl-celilo.title: Oregon Encyclopedia, Celilo Falls
g5-pl-celilo.notes: Regional history synthesizes 11,000 years of occupation, fisheries, later treaty rights and flooding; detailed nineteenth-century rights must not be projected unaltered into 1200 CE.

g5-pl-knudson.title: Ruthann Knudson, Fish, Roots, Game and Trade in the Columbia Plateau, Journal of Forestry 78(9) (1980)
g5-pl-knudson.notes: Public abstract addresses camas, salmon, seasonal settlements and stewardship; full paper not reviewed.

g5-pl-council.title: Northwest Power and Conservation Council, Indian Fishing (Columbia River history)
g5-pl-council.notes: Regional documentary synthesis distinguishes evidence for early fishing from later drying and historically documented fishing regulations.

g5-ba-museum.title: National Museum of Korea, Balhae Kingdom exhibition overview
g5-ba-museum.notes: Public artifact/context descriptions of Balhae dates, capitals, exchanges with Silla, Tang and Japan. Museum national-history framing must be read critically.

g5-ba-epitaph.title: Jung Hyun-Sook, Calligraphic Styles of the Epitaphs of Princess Jeonghe and Princess Jeonghyo (2009)
g5-ba-epitaph.notes: Scholarly English abstract comparing two named Balhae royal women’s epitaphs and their script styles; text is not directly quoted.

g5-ba-royal.title: Park Yu Jeong, The Form and Structure of Epitaphs of Balhae Royal Women (2026)
g5-ba-royal.notes: Academic abstract compares four royal women’s epitaphs; notes formulaic virtues and limits on biographies; full article not reviewed.

g5-ba-diaspora.title: Kwon Ohyoung, Archaeological Evidence of the Diaspora of Balhae Displaced People (2023)
g5-ba-diaspora.notes: Scholarly abstract on burial evidence following 926, distinguishing archaeological similarity from fixed ethnic identity.

g5-go-unesco.title: UNESCO Memory of the World, Printing Woodblocks of the Tripitaka Koreana and Miscellaneous Buddhist Scriptures
g5-go-unesco.notes: Institutional register describes 81,258 Goryeo-era blocks, preservation at Haeinsa and wider manuscript/translating traditions. Heritage nomination is not a complete labor ledger.

g5-go-met.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Korea, 1000–1400 CE timeline
g5-go-met.notes: Museum chronology on first and second Goryeo Tripitaka projects, war, Buddhist patronage, paper and ink, movable type and painting; chronology is synthesized.

g5-go-nmk.title: National Museum of Korea, Buddhist Scriptures Printed from the Second Tripitaka Koreana Woodblocks
g5-go-nmk.notes: Museum object description distinguishes first and second Tripitaka projects and the Tripitaka Bureau, war context and subsequent prints.

g5-go-asian.title: Smithsonian/Asian Art Museum publications, Goryeo Buddhist art and printing
g5-go-asian.notes: Academic exhibition chapter excerpt on Buddhist images, woodblock projects and material production; published interpretive essay not craftsperson diary.

g5-mu-unesco.title: UNESCO Memory of the World, Collection of Documents from Mount Mugh
g5-mu-unesco.notes: 2025 institutional entry describes Devashtich, 722 conflict, multilingual records and marriage contract; register summary, not independent document edition.

g5-mu-iranica.title: Gregory Semenov, Mount Mugh, Encyclopaedia Iranica
g5-mu-iranica.notes: Specialist encyclopedia on excavated fortress, archive discovery and early eighth-century documents; chronology and political interpretations reflect published research.

g5-mu-marriage.title: Ilya Yakubovich, Sogdian Marriage Contract, Encyclopaedia Iranica
g5-mu-marriage.notes: Scholarly edited analysis of Sogdian marriage document Nov.3 and Nov.4, names Ot-tegin and Chat and dating c. 709/710; document’s legal terms represent an arrangement, not universal custom.

g5-mu-smith.title: Pavel Lurje, The Castle on Mount Mugh and Its Documents, Smithsonian Sogdians
g5-mu-smith.notes: Specialist public snippet discusses discovery and conflicting alliances; full page access blocked during review.

g5-af-nli.title: National Library of Israel, The Afghan Genizah collection overview
g5-af-nli.notes: Holding institution overview of 11th–13th-century documents, Abu Nasr family, merchant account book, Hebrew/Persian/Arabic materials; reported discovery context is incomplete.

g5-af-thorpe.title: Samuel Thrope and Ofir Haim, A Jewish Family on the Silk Road: The Afghan Genizah, NLI Treasures
g5-af-thorpe.notes: Inspected library publication and page image: document Ms. Heb. 4° 8333.216 acknowledges seven shiyani owed to Abu Nasr b. Daniyal, dated May 1011 in Bamiyan; English rendering is the editors’.

d6-lci-clave.title: Elsa Clavé and Arlo Griffiths, The Laguna Copperplate Inscription: Tenth-Century Luzon, Java, and the Malay World, Philippine Studies 70 (2022)
d6-lci-clave.notes: 2022 epigraphic re-edition, Old Malay grammar and loanwords, named parties and debt-clearance; the article abstract and excerpts including a segment of the new translation were inspected. Earlier Postma readings remain influential; legal status is an editorial interpretation.

d6-lci-nmp.title: National Museum of the Philippines, Cultural Exchange between the Philippine Islands and Maritime Asia
d6-lci-nmp.notes: Shaka 822 / 900 CE, Kawi-type script and context alongside Butuan archaeology; brief public museum synthesis, not a primary critical edition.

d6-mad-crowther.title: Alison Crowther et al., Ancient crops provide first archaeological signature of the westward Austronesian expansion, PNAS 113 (2016)
d6-mad-crowther.notes: Open-access archaeobotanical research on rice and other Asian crops in Madagascar and the Comoros, its sampling limitations and migration models; sites are not a complete census of earliest arrivals.

d6-mad-genetics.title: Genetic evidence and historical theories of the Asian and African origins of the present Malagasy population, 2021 review
d6-mad-genetics.notes: Review abstract supports African and Asian population ancestry and uncertainty about migration routes and timing; genetic ancestry does not directly identify language or individual voyages.

d6-jp-toji.title: Kyoto University Rare Materials Digital Archive, Kyō-ō Gokokuji Documents
d6-jp-toji.notes: Collection description of 3043 documents concerning Tōji estates, annual accounts and temple organization, covering several periods; archival survival is selective.

d6-jp-todai.title: University of Tokyo BiblioPlaza, Tōdaiji documents collection
d6-jp-todai.notes: More than 10,000 temple-related historical documents, many undated or reorganized in later collections; not a rural household census.

d6-jp-maps.title: University of Zurich, Old Japanese Maps: Heian, Kamakura and Muromachi estate maps
d6-jp-maps.notes: Research tutorial on shōen rights, tax exemptions, imperial/provincial estates, and medieval estate map conventions; interpretive secondary overview.

d6-jp-ito.title: Land Administration in Medieval Japan: Ito no shō in Chikuzen Province, 1131–1336, Historical Research
d6-jp-ito.notes: Specialist study abstract supports shifting Kyushu estate administration and regional manager influence; full detailed article was not inspected.

d6-jp-land.title: Land Transactions and Land Holding in Medieval Japan: Local Ownership Structure, Shigaku Zasshi
d6-jp-land.notes: Study abstract based on Tōji Kuze estate records and differentiated local landholding; do not generalize percentages to all Japan.

d6-ife-met.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Ife (from ca. 6th Century)
d6-ife-met.notes: Overview of Ilé-Ifẹ̀ archaeology, Yoruba sacred history and the 1200–1500 art tradition; community historical traditions and archaeological chronologies must be distinguished.

d6-ife-paving.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Ife Pre-Pavement and Pavement Era (800–1000 A.D.)
d6-ife-paving.notes: Art-historical organization of archaeological periods, ceramic paving associated with growth of urban spaces; period labels are scholarly conventions.

d6-ife-terra.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Ife Terracottas (1000–1400 A.D.)
d6-ife-terra.notes: Terracotta and copper alloy artistic traditions; caution against uncritically projecting later gendered craft divisions backward.

d6-ife-british.title: British Museum, Brass head from Wunmonije Compound, Ife, collection Af1939,34.1
d6-ife-british.notes: Object record: cast brass, probable 14th to early 15th century, found 1938; specific identification and original function unknown.

d6-ife-food.title: Early archaeological evidence of wheat and cotton from medieval Ile-Ife, Nigeria, PNAS (2024)
d6-ife-food.notes: Scholarly article excerpt indicates archaeobotanical wheat and cotton finds in medieval Ilé-Ifẹ̀; the crops cannot supply a population-wide diet or trade census.

d6-ife-urban.title: Akinwumi Ogundiran, A Mosaic of Yorùbá Ontology and Materiality of Pleasure Since AD 1000, African Studies Review
d6-ife-urban.notes: Archaeological interpretation of early Yoruba urbanism, material culture and city-scale economic life; selected excerpt rather than full article.

d6-map-unesco.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Mapungubwe Cultural Landscape
d6-map-unesco.notes: UNESCO landscape chronology, K2 and Mapungubwe settlement shifts, trade and differentiated social spaces; its climate explanation is an interpretation, not proof of a single cause.

d6-map-sanparks.title: South African National Parks, Mapungubwe: Natural and Cultural History
d6-map-sanparks.notes: Public account of 1932 rediscovery, named local participant Mowena and subsequent excavations; historic rediscovery narrative may be incomplete.

d6-map-steyn.title: Maryna Steyn, The Mapungubwe gold graves revisited, South African Archaeological Bulletin (2007)
d6-map-steyn.notes: Archival reappraisal of Mapungubwe gold burials emphasizes missing 1930s excavation evidence and interpretive uncertainty; abstract reviewed.

d6-map-met.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Mapungubwe (ca. 1050–1270)
d6-map-met.notes: Material and archaeological summary of gold grave goods, social differentiation and regional exchange; museum synthesis.

d6-map-duffey.title: Alexander Edward Duffey, Mapungubwe: Interpretation of the Gold Content of Original Gold Burial M1 (2012)
d6-map-duffey.notes: Alternative reconstruction of gold foil ornaments and their possible original arrangement; presented as a hypothesis, not settled function.

d6-but-nmp.title: National Museum of the Philippines, Preserving Our Heritage Towards the Future of Our Museums (Butuan boat fieldwork)
d6-but-nmp.notes: Institutional summary of Butuan boat findspots, later first-millennium dates and continuing fieldwork; dates differ across studies and vessels.

d6-but-lacsina.title: Ligaya S. P. Lacsina, From the Site to the Museum: Butuan Boat Remains Displayed in the National Museum of the Philippines (2022)
d6-but-lacsina.notes: Specialist excavation and curation account; excerpt documents conflicting early radiocarbon descriptions and revised measurements for individual boats.

d6-but-profile.title: University of the Philippines, Ligaya S. P. Lacsina, maritime archaeology research profile
d6-but-profile.notes: University source confirming Lacsina publications and Butuan boat construction focus; research profile, not an independent vessel-date assessment.

d6-but-nmp2.title: National Museum of the Philippines, Early Maritime Exchange and the Butuan Boats
d6-but-nmp2.notes: National Museum summary of lashed-lug vessels and maritime links, alongside Laguna inscription; broad overview, not individual boat inventory.

d6-tich-2026.title: Revisiting Tichitt: New Dates and Data from the 1968 Excavations by Patrick Munson, Azania (2026)
d6-tich-2026.notes: 2026 specialist reassessment using 14 AMS dates on curated excavation charcoal samples; improved chronology still reveals large evidentiary gaps.

d6-tich-2022.title: Spatial Organization and Socio-Economic Differentiation at the Dhar Tichitt Center of Dakhlet el Atrouss I, African Archaeological Review (2022)
d6-tich-2022.notes: Detailed archaeological account of drystone compounds, millet, cattle, social differentiation hypotheses, and long chronology; interpretations of status remain provisional.

d6-kl-yurok.title: Yurok Tribe, Our History
d6-kl-yurok.notes: Yurok-authored account of lower Klamath home, fishing, crafts, river responsibilities and continuity; does not specify the exact date of every documented practice.

d6-kl-karuk.title: Karuk Tribe Department of Natural Resources, Tribal Fisheries
d6-kl-karuk.notes: Karuk account of Spring Salmon Ceremony and fishing responsibilities at Ameekyáaraam; community interpretation should not be reduced to one ecological effect.

d6-kl-paper.title: Indigenous Systems of Management for Culturally and Ecologically Resilient Pacific Salmon Fisheries (2021)
d6-kl-paper.notes: Open synthesis of Indigenous fisheries management, Klamath weir use and conservation practice; mixes historical and ethnographic sources requiring chronological care.

d6-kl-smith.title: Smithsonian National Museum of American History, Hupa and Yurok: Salmon Coast
d6-kl-smith.notes: Exhibit on historical Hupa and Yurok fisheries, weirs and modern continuity; broad synthesis, not a 1400 CE eyewitness account.

d6-kl-fish.title: Archaeological Perspectives on Native American Fisheries of California with Emphasis on Steelhead and Salmon (2004)
d6-kl-fish.notes: Study of archaeological reconstruction and limits of historic fish distributions; literature excerpt, no site-specific quantitative claims applied.

d7-ph-met.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, The Phoenicians (1500-300 B.C.), Heilbrunn Timeline (2004)
d7-ph-met.notes: Coastal city geography, material crafts, networks and Carthaginian connections. A museum-level historical synthesis, not an archaeological site report.

d7-ph-language.title: Maria Giulia Amadasi Guzzo, The Language, Oxford Handbook of the Phoenician and Punic Mediterranean (2019)
d7-ph-language.notes: Phoenician and Punic language, chronology and consonantal script. Only public chapter abstract inspected; specific philological arguments remain to be checked in full text.

d7-ph-early.title: Nadav Naaman, Egyptian Centres and the Distribution of the Alphabet in the Levant, Tel Aviv 47 (2020)
d7-ph-early.notes: Proposed interpretation of alphabetic development in Egyptian-Levantine contact zones; scholarly argument, not settled chronology. Full text access restricted.

d7-ph-spread.title: Andre Lemaire, The Spread of Alphabetic Scripts (c. 1700-500 BCE), Diogenes 55 (2008)
d7-ph-spread.notes: Review of early alphabetic forms before Phoenician and subsequent branches; detailed evidence not fully inspected.

d7-ph-kai.title: Digital Epigraphy and Archaeology Project, Ohio State University, KAI 002 Phoenician tomb inscription
d7-ph-kai.notes: Inscription and epigraphic context from Byblos tomb; individual dating and paleography remain scholarly interpretations.

d7-ph-carthage.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Western North Africa 1000 B.C.-1 A.D., Heilbrunn Timeline
d7-ph-carthage.notes: Carthaginian chronology, trade, Roman conquest; foundation date explicitly traditional; not a population history.

d7-ph-stelae.title: British Museum, Catalogue of Punic Stelae in the British Museum (collection publication)
d7-ph-stelae.notes: Collection-level description of Punic votive inscriptions; does not resolve disputed tophet interpretations.

d7-ij-merneptah.title: Teach Jewish History, Ancient Israel and Judah: teaching supplement and source guide
d7-ij-merneptah.notes: Early Merneptah identification and links to named artifacts; educational synthesis, not an original Egyptian text edition.

d7-ij-teldan.title: The Jewish Museum and Israel Museum, Tel Dan Stele exhibition record (2024-2025)
d7-ij-teldan.notes: Ninth-century Aramaic royal inscription referencing the House of David; does not substantiate a detailed biblical biography or tenth-century territorial extent.

d7-ij-mesha.title: Musee du Louvre, Stele de Mesha, collection AO 5066
d7-ij-mesha.notes: Ninth-century Moabite victory inscription; a ruler's self-serving claim, not neutral political history.

d7-ij-senn.title: Israel Museum, The Assyrian Campaign in Judah as told in the Sennacherib Prism (2025 exhibition)
d7-ij-senn.notes: 691 BCE Akkadian prism recounting 701 BCE campaign; royal self-presentation, not an independent account of the entire war.

d7-ij-lachish.title: David Ussishkin, The Lachish Reliefs, in Assyria to Iberia scholarship
d7-ij-lachish.notes: Lachish archaeological evidence and Assyrian palace reliefs; excerpt reviewed, not a full independent reading of excavation volumes.

d7-ij-babylon.title: Posen Library, Babylonian Chronicle: Entry for 598/97 BCE
d7-ij-babylon.notes: Translation of Nebuchadnezzar's 597 BCE capture of Jerusalem, in a restricted entry with visible opening lines; limited in scope.

d7-sr-haryono.title: Timbul Haryono, Traces of Buddhism in Sumatra: An Archaeological Perspective, UNESCO Silk Roads resource
d7-sr-haryono.notes: Summarizes Kedukan Bukit, Talang Tuwo, Kota Kapur and related inscription debates; older archaeological synthesis, not full critical editions.

d7-sr-inscriptions.title: I. Sri Vijaya, Bulletin de l'Ecole francaise d'Extreme-Orient 40 (1940)
d7-sr-inscriptions.notes: Early scholarly text discussion of dated Palembang inscriptions; interpretations and date conversion have been revised subsequently.

d7-sr-state.title: Hermann Kulke, Srivijaya Revisited: Reflections on State Formation of a Southeast Asian Thalassocracy, BEFEO 102 (2016)
d7-sr-state.notes: Changing state formation, maritime networks and the uncertainty of Chola raid motives; scholarly synthesis, interpretations contested.

d7-sr-yijing.title: Qin Dashu and Chong Yuan Chien, The Record of Sribijaya from a Great Visitor, international seminar proceedings
d7-sr-yijing.notes: Yijing's reported visits and Buddhist textual scholarship; excerpt viewed through searchable result, full proceedings not systematically checked.

d7-sr-chola.title: Hermann Kulke, The Naval Expeditions of the Cholas in the Context of Asian History (2009)
d7-sr-chola.notes: Discusses the 1025 Chola claims from royal inscriptions; motives and raid consequences debated; chapter text not completely accessed.

d7-jp-shirane.title: Haruo Shirane, Introduction: Court Culture, Women, and the Rise of Vernacular Literature, Cambridge History of Japanese Literature (2016)
d7-jp-shirane.notes: Elite court writing, vernacular literature, kana, provincial power and authorship; only the public chapter summary accessed.

d7-jp-women.title: Women's Writing in the Japanese Heian Period, in Women's Literary Cultures in the Global Middle Ages (2023)
d7-jp-women.notes: Murasaki, Sei Shonagon, Kagero Diary and author-patron relationship; summary only, no manuscript-critical edition.

d7-jp-scroll.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Japanese Illustrated Handscrolls (2012)
d7-jp-scroll.notes: Genji composition and later illustrated reception; artistic interpretations from later centuries cannot serve as direct observations of eleventh-century court.

d7-jp-genji.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Illustrated Handscrolls of The Tale of Genji, collection 839905
d7-jp-genji.notes: Sixteenth-century Genji illustrations preserve a later visual and manuscript tradition; not an autograph by Murasaki.

d7-ig-met.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Igbo-Ukwu (ca. 9th Century), Heilbrunn Timeline (2001)
d7-ig-met.notes: Object range and technical practices; its ninth-century label is not decisive given more recent chronometric work.

d7-ig-reappraisal.title: Susan Keech McIntosh, Igbo-Ukwu at 50: A Symposium on Recent Archaeological Research and Analysis, African Archaeological Review 39 (2022)
d7-ig-reappraisal.notes: Find histories, three excavation locations, bead provenance and newer high-precision dates; web indexing exposed detailed excerpts, full page intermittently blocked.

d7-ig-metals.title: Quanyu Wang, Paul Craddock and Julie Hudson, Metallographic study of objects from Igbo Isaiah, British Museum research (2022)
d7-ig-metals.notes: Technical study of copper-alloy fragments, mostly lost-wax castings and limitations of pre-excavation collecting; abstract inspected.

d7-ig-local.title: A Multivocal Case Study of Decoloniality in Archaeological Exploration in Igbo-Ukwu, Nigeria (1938-2024)
d7-ig-local.notes: Recorded local family accounts of discovery and collection, to be assessed alongside excavation records; public excerpts inspected.

d7-ig-old-dates.title: Babatunde Lawal, Dating Problems at Igbo-Ukwu, Journal of African History 14 (1973)
d7-ig-old-dates.notes: Historical dispute over ninth-century dating, earlier critique not current chronometric consensus; abstract inspected.

d7-ig-provenance.title: J. E. G. Sutton, The international factor at Igbo-Ukwu, Smithsonian Libraries catalog
d7-ig-provenance.notes: Hypotheses on local metal sourcing and longer-distance bead exchange; speculative trade routes should not be treated as proven.

d7-ma-dresden.title: Saxon State and University Library Dresden, The Dresden Maya Codex: Content
d7-ma-dresden.notes: Calendars, Venus table, eclipse tables, ritual imagery; institutional guide, with individual glyph readings still subject to scholarship.

d7-ma-loc.title: Library of Congress, The Dresden Codex, World Digital Library item 2021667917
d7-ma-loc.notes: Codex material, acquisition, format, survival and content; summarizing catalogue, not critical edition.

d7-ma-inah.title: INAH Mexico, Codice Maya de Mexico research and conservation project (2017-2018)
d7-ma-inah.notes: Research authentication, early Postclassic dating, collecting and looting history; project-level interpretive account.

d7-ma-venus.title: Gerardo Aldana, Discovering Discovery: Chichen Itza, the Dresden Codex Venus Table and Tenth-Century Maya Astronomical Innovation (2016)
d7-ma-venus.notes: Study of Venus table relations to ritual and historical context; proposed specific readings require comparison with other Mayanists.

d7-ma-math.title: Dilucidando el lenguaje visual de la Tabla de Venus del Codice de Dresde, Estudios de Cultura Maya (2020)
d7-ma-math.notes: Mathematical calendar structure and iconography of Venus table; reconstruction, not an ancient authorial commentary.

d7-ki-nist.title: National Institute of Standards and Technology, Standardizing an Empire: Inka Khipu (2023)
d7-ki-nist.notes: Decimal knot notation, cord construction, twist and color; explanation is a modern decoding, not access to every cord's original labels.

d7-ki-pur.title: Gary Urton and Carrie J. Brezine, Khipu Accounting in Ancient Peru, Science 309 (2005)
d7-ki-pur.notes: Study of 21 Puruchuco khipu and hierarchical aggregation of accounting information; only abstract inspected.

d7-ki-wari.title: Gary Urton, From Middle Horizon Cord-Keeping to the Rise of Inka Khipus, Antiquity 88 (2014)
d7-ki-wari.notes: AMS dates and suggested quinary groupings of Wari-era khipu; proposed system interpretation not confirmed for every artifact.

d7-ki-oxford.title: Manuel Medrano and Galen Brokaw, Quipu, Oxford Bibliographies in Latin American Studies (updated 2023)
d7-ki-oxford.notes: Distinguishes Inka, Wari and colonial records and broader encoding possibilities; not a decipherment of nonnumeric strings.

d7-zh-wade.title: Geoff Wade, Zheng He and Ming China's Voyages in the Early 15th Century, Oxford Research Encyclopedia (2020)
d7-zh-wade.notes: Voyage period, state objectives, military interventions, East African range and later politics; chapter abstract only.

d7-zh-dreyer.title: Edward L. Dreyer, Zheng He: China and the Oceans in the Early Ming Dynasty, 1405-1433 (2007), Smithsonian library catalog
d7-zh-dreyer.notes: Book table of contents identifies voyages, inscriptions, Ma Huan and ship-size debates; full monograph not accessed.

d7-zh-inscription.title: Zheng He, Liujiagang Inscription (1431), English translation in Historical Accounts of Zheng He source collection
d7-zh-inscription.notes: Source-reader excerpt establishes commissioned voyages, public commemoration and heavenly protection; rhetorical primary text, not neutral fleet manifest.

d7-zh-size.title: Notes on maritime ship size and Liujiagang/Changle inscriptions, University of Pittsburgh open book (2024)
d7-zh-size.notes: Notes distinguish 1431 inscription reference to more than 100 ships from contested huge ship dimensions; supplementary, not full analysis.

d8-ur-cdli.title: CDLI, AAS 035 (P100023), Ur III female laborers and monthly rations
d8-ur-cdli.notes: Transliteration and editorial English gloss for one Umma tablet; this single account cannot establish workers’ legal status, actual diet or life history.

d8-ur-catalog.title: CDLI, Neo-Sumerian administrative texts from Umma kept in the British Museum, Part Five
d8-ur-catalog.notes: Catalogue and brief descriptions across many Ur III tablets; entries are not a substitute for fully edited primary texts.

d8-ur-iris.title: Some Ur III Texts from Irisagrig in the Iraq Museum, 2020, Liverpool repository
d8-ur-iris.notes: Abstract describes women wool-plucking, canal work and rations in seven tablets; full article not independently inspected.

d8-at-arist.title: Constitution of the Athenians, chapter 42, translated primary text, MIT Classics
d8-at-arist.notes: Late fourth-century perspective conventionally associated with Aristotle; describes a particular constitutional period, not all of Athens’ history.

d8-at-sep.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Aristotle’s Political Theory
d8-at-sep.notes: Explains Aristotle’s concept of citizen and the exclusions of Athenian democracy; distinguish philosopher’s normative claims from social facts.

d8-at-metics.title: Foundation of the Hellenic World, Classical Period: Social Sources, translated extracts
d8-at-metics.notes: Short English excerpts of Xenophon and Aristotle illuminate metics and slaves; selections cannot measure all social experience.

d8-sa-unesco.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Landmarks of the Ancient Kingdom of Saba, Marib
d8-sa-unesco.notes: Site-level chronology, irrigation, monuments and inscriptions; heritage account is not a critical edition of individual texts.

d8-sa-smith.title: Smithsonian National Museum of Asian Art, Excavations: Awam Temple
d8-sa-smith.notes: Accounts for the site and its 1951 excavation; modern Queen of Sheba associations are traditions, not authenticated ruler identifications.

d8-te-inah-neighbors.title: INAH, The Foreign Neighborhoods of Teotihuacan: A City of Many Cultures
d8-te-inah-neighbors.notes: Institutional interpretation of multi-origin neighborhoods; precise population, ethnic affiliations and political functions remain inferential.

d8-te-inah-end.title: INAH, The Story of a Collapse: The End of Great Teotihuacan
d8-te-inah-end.notes: Describes selective fires, migration and reuse; archaeological chronology and motives for destruction remain debated.

d8-te-cowgill.title: George L. Cowgill, Ancient Teotihuacan, Cambridge University Press, chapter summaries
d8-te-cowgill.notes: Scholarly book excerpts cover population, urbanism and debated end dates; not full chapter coverage.

d8-ab-primary.title: Why Do We Translate? Arabic Sources on Translation, primary texts with editorial introductions
d8-ab-primary.notes: Gives Hunayn’s epistle context and later bibliographers; distinct genres, retrospective sources and translation histories must be distinguished.

d8-ab-sep.title: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy, Greek Sources in Arabic and Islamic Philosophy
d8-ab-sep.notes: Documents translation networks and philosophical texts; focuses particularly on philosophical transmission rather than the whole scholarly economy.

d8-ab-chicago.title: In a Clear Arabic Tongue: Arabic and the Making of a Science-Language Regime
d8-ab-chicago.notes: Historical analysis of Arabic science and competing explanations for translation; attributive arguments should not be treated as consensus.

d8-so-walton.title: Linda Walton, Schooling, State, and Society in Song and Jin, Cambridge 2023
d8-so-walton.notes: Chapter abstract on schooling, examination recruitment and print; complete chapter not independently inspected.

d8-so-gentry.title: The State, the Gentry, and Local Institutions: The Song Dynasty and Long-Term Trends
d8-so-gentry.notes: Documents geographically unequal mobility and local elite institutions; not a complete census of Song families.

d8-so-women.title: Picturing Parental Love for Girls in Song (960–1279) China, Journal of Chinese History
d8-so-women.notes: Epitaphs and literary evidence illuminate elite women and girls; cannot generalize automatically to all households.

d8-so-loc.title: Library of Congress, Dong dou shi lue, Song edition woodblocks and later impression
d8-so-loc.notes: Catalogue distinguishes first Song blocks from later impressions; not evidence of universal publishing controls.

d8-mg-uk.title: UK Parliament, Magna Carta overview and significance
d8-mg-uk.notes: Introductory synthesis; later constitutional significance must be distinguished from the 1215 baronial bargain.

d8-mg-archives.title: UK National Archives, Magna Carta 1214–1225, primary documents and contextual notes
d8-mg-archives.notes: Shows different royal orders, charters and translated selections; particular documents and versions must be named.

d8-mg-bodleian.title: Bodleian Libraries, Legal History: Magna Carta and revised versions
d8-mg-bodleian.notes: Legal chronology of surviving issues and revised texts; guide, not a critical edition of the whole archive.

d8-mg-loc.title: Library of Congress, Magna Carta: Confirmation by Kings and Parliament
d8-mg-loc.notes: Displays transmission and omission across reissues; exhibition descriptions do not establish later universal rights in 1215.

d8-wa-met.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Central and Southern Andes 500–1000 AD
d8-wa-met.notes: Chronology and regional spread of Wari and Tiwanaku; estimates and old dates are subject to later research.

d8-wa-met-essay.title: José Ochatoma Paravicino, Wari Imperial Art, Metropolitan Museum of Art, 2025
d8-wa-met-essay.notes: Separates Wari and Tiwanaku political histories and related imagery; art-historical emphasis.

d8-wa-pik.title: Gordon F. McEwan, Pikillacta: The Wari Empire in Cuzco, Smithsonian Libraries record
d8-wa-pik.notes: Book description outlines archaeology and planning at Pikillacta; detailed results not independently consulted.

d8-wa-unesco.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Tiwanaku: Spiritual and Political Centre
d8-wa-unesco.notes: Monuments and raised fields; site-level institutional narrative may overstate uniform rule or precise numerical estimates.

d8-wa-survey.title: New insights into prehispanic urban organization at Tiwanaku, 2019 archaeological survey
d8-wa-survey.notes: Survey abstract establishes dense settlement, terracing and water-related features; individual construction phases remain under study.

d8-wa-cambridge.title: Water, Huacas, and Ancestor Worship: Traces of a Sacred Wari Landscape
d8-wa-cambridge.notes: Drought and water-related religious expansion are proposed explanations, not settled motives for all Wari actions.

d9-oz-inah.title: INAH, The Tombs of Monte Albán
d9-oz-inah.notes: Site chronology, burial contexts and tomb paintings; an institutional summary, not an edition of every inscription.

d9-oz-met.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Monte Albán, essays on city and stone sculpture
d9-oz-met.notes: Relates political images and glyphs to stone sculpture; readings of some signs and ruler identifications remain debated.

d9-oz-uofm.title: Joyce Marcus, Origins of Hieroglyphic Writing, Archaeological Research in Oaxaca, University of Michigan
d9-oz-uofm.notes: Original archaeological research and epigraphic proposals; not every Zapotec sign is securely deciphered.

d9-oz-arch.title: Cerro Tilcajete, a secondary center of the early Zapotec state, Revista Arqueología, INAH
d9-oz-arch.notes: Abstract describes regional settlement hierarchy and local variation; full excavation results not separately inspected.

d9-law-quittance.title: Geoffrey Khan, An Arabic Legal Document from the Umayyad Period, 1994
d9-law-quittance.notes: Publishes the Jamīla quittance and seven dinars; publisher extract has inconsistent AH/CE date notation, cross-checked as AH 88/707 CE in Khan’s later discussion.

d9-law-tillier.title: Mathieu Tillier, Dispensing Justice in a Minority Context: Upper Egypt in the early eighth century
d9-law-tillier.notes: Qurra-Basilios judicial letters show governor involvement; only incoming official orders survive, not all litigation outcomes.

d9-law-khan.title: Geoffrey Khan, Opening Formula and Witness Clauses in Arabic Legal Documents, 2019
d9-law-khan.notes: Abstract contrasts early Arabic and Greek/Coptic documentary forms; formal detail should be checked against full article.

d9-so-litigation.title: Yu-Hsuan Wong, Remarried Women in Song-Dynasty Litigation, Institute of History and Philology
d9-so-litigation.notes: Summary of Zhao Zongji case in Qingming Ji, not a representative rate of women’s success in courts.

d9-so-birge.title: Bettine Birge, Women, Property, and Confucian Reaction in Sung and Yüan China, Cambridge University Press
d9-so-birge.notes: Book and chapter summaries argue for stronger Song women’s property protections; full monograph not reviewed.

d9-so-inherit.title: Takahashi and Fraleigh, Orphaned Daughters: Property Rights in the Southern Song, 2015
d9-so-inherit.notes: Challenges a generalized inheritance-rights interpretation; scholarship remains contested and context-specific.

d9-so-ci.title: Daniel Asen, Song Ci (1186–1249) and the modern history of forensic medicine
d9-so-ci.notes: Identifies Xiyuan jilu and warns that Song Ci’s modern founder image is a later construction; not evidence of universal period practice.

d9-gold-mould.title: S. Nixon and colleagues, New Light on the Early Islamic West African Gold Trade: Coin Moulds from Tadmekka
d9-gold-mould.notes: Ninth-tenth-century moulds interpreted as evidence of gold pellet coinage; scale and makers’ identities remain unknown.

d9-gold-glass.title: Th. Rehren and S. Nixon, Refining Gold with Glass: Tadmekka, Mali, Journal of Archaeological Science
d9-gold-glass.notes: Two crucible fragments support local glass-assisted refining; they cannot measure aggregate trade volumes.

d9-gold-gao.title: Takezawa and Cisse, Discovery of the Earliest Royal Palace in Gao, Cahiers d’études africaines
d9-gold-gao.notes: Gao Saney and stone-building excavation summary; architectural function and precise period interpretations can be revised.

d9-gold-inscr.title: The Oldest Extant Writing of West Africa: Medieval Epigraphs from Issuk, Saney and Egeg-n-Tawaqqast, Smithsonian record
d9-gold-inscr.notes: Bibliographic abstract of seven inscriptions; direct inscription editions and translations not independently checked.

d9-kilwa-deposit.title: John Perkins, Jeffrey Fleisher, and Stephanie Wynne-Jones, A Deposit of Kilwa-Type Coins from Songo Mnara, 2014
d9-kilwa-deposit.notes: Over 300 copper coins in dated house foundations; ritual meaning is an interpretation, not a recorded intention.

d9-kilwa-coins.title: Stephanie Wynne-Jones and Jeffrey Fleisher, Coins in Context, Cambridge Archaeological Journal, 2012
d9-kilwa-coins.notes: Treats coins as monetary and socially meaningful objects; abstract cannot establish full regional circulation rates.

d9-kilwa-unesco.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Ruins of Kilwa Kisiwani and Ruins of Songo Mnara
d9-kilwa-unesco.notes: Site chronology, mosques and port trade; the UNESCO summary is not a town-wide economic census.

d9-kilwa-oxford.title: Oxford Research Encyclopedia, Kilwa and its Environs
d9-kilwa-oxford.notes: Describes coastal commerce and development from 11th to 15th centuries; full chapter not reviewed.

d9-timb-uct.title: University of Cape Town Tombouctou Manuscripts Project, Timbuktu’s History
d9-timb-uct.notes: Dates development as intellectual center primarily to fifteenth century; later scholar Ahmad Baba must not be moved before 1500.

d9-timb-unesco.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Timbuktu
d9-timb-unesco.notes: Broad fifteen-sixteenth century city history, with institutional terms and numerical claims not independently corroborated.

d9-timb-cambridge.title: Charles Stewart and collaborators, What’s in the Manuscripts of Timbuktu? History in Africa
d9-timb-cambridge.notes: Inventory of 31 libraries reveals many undated/recent manuscripts; conclusions apply to surveyed holdings, not every collection.

d9-timb-loc.title: Library of Congress, Timbuktu: An Islamic Cultural Center, Islamic Manuscripts from Mali
d9-timb-loc.notes: Documents manuscript subjects and custody; cataloged objects vary by copy date and cannot all be placed in the fifteenth century.

d9-ben-nms.title: National Museums Scotland, The Court Arts and History of the Kingdom of Benin
d9-ben-nms.notes: Clearly labels Ogiso/Oranmiyan history as oral traditions; court chronology and objects differ in dates.

d9-ben-prm.title: Pitt Rivers Museum, University of Oxford, The Kingdom of Benin
d9-ben-prm.notes: Geography and trade; summary spans centuries and later features must not automatically be backdated pre-1500.

d9-ben-met.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Edo Ivory and Wood Carving Guilds, Vessel
d9-ben-met.notes: Court craft and regional trade; much extant court art is from after 1500, not a contemporaneous view of early Benin.

d9-maya-tikal.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Tikal: Stone Sculpture
d9-maya-tikal.notes: Stelae, early inscriptions and lineage; later ruler claims of distant ancestors require separate dating.

d9-maya-chron.title: Metropolitan Museum of Art, Maya Area, 500–1000 CE, Chronology
d9-maya-chron.notes: Dates Tikal, Palenque, Calakmul and Copán; political relationships and attribution remain revisable.

d9-maya-doyle.title: James Doyle, A Maya Game of Thrones and Artistic Innovation, Metropolitan Museum of Art
d9-maya-doyle.notes: Explains rival courts and dynastic political display; analogy with fiction is illustrative, not historical evidence.

m10-meroe-unesco.title: Archaeological Sites of the Island of Meroe — UNESCO World Heritage Centre
m10-meroe-unesco.notes: Heritage synthesis of excavated royal, urban, industrial, religious and hydraulic sites. Dated details apply to selected components; does not prove national production totals.

m10-meroe-natakamani.title: National Museum (Czech Republic), Building programme of King Natakamani and Queen Amanitore
m10-meroe-natakamani.notes: Archaeological project account of Wad Ben Naga, Amun and Mut buildings and paired bilingual names; script decipherment is not complete language translation.

m10-meroe-trade.title: The Meroitic Empire: Trade and Cultural Influences in an Indian Ocean Context — African Archaeological Review (2014)
m10-meroe-trade.notes: Research on exchange and religious sites; relied on accessible research summary, not independently reanalyzed finds.

m10-khmer-lustig.title: Eileen Lustig, Power and Pragmatism in the Political Economy of Angkor (University of Sydney, 2009)
m10-khmer-lustig.notes: Publisher landing-page extracts plus selected thesis discussion on land grants and overlapping rights. Interpretations of legal terms require attention to specific Khmer inscriptions; full critical editions not rechecked.

m10-khmer-officials.title: Eileen Lustig and Terry Lustig, Losing Ground: Decline of Angkor's Middle-Level Officials (2019)
m10-khmer-officials.notes: Abstract and publisher synopsis only. Changing appearances of vāp and loñ are an authorial interpretation of inscriptions, not demographic census.

m10-khmer-sdok.title: Chhany Sak-Humphry, The Sdok Kak Thom Inscription with a Grammatical Analysis of Old Khmer
m10-khmer-sdok.notes: University scholarly description of inscription, bilingual composition, edition and translation; not the full translated stele.

m10-kongo-thornton.title: John Thornton, The Emergence of Social and Political Complexity in West Central Africa (2025)
m10-kongo-thornton.notes: Research article reviewing later oral traditions and early documentation. Mpemba predecessor and consolidation sequence are scholarly reconstructions, not contemporaneous fourteenth-century records.

m10-kongo-unesco.title: Mbanza Kongo: Vestiges of the Capital of the former Kingdom of Kongo — UNESCO World Heritage Centre
m10-kongo-unesco.notes: Heritage synthesis of the capital site over many phases. Surviving masonry and colonial documentation postdate pre-contact settlement.

m10-australia-willandra.title: Willandra Lakes Region — UNESCO World Heritage Centre
m10-australia-willandra.notes: Archaeological and geoenvironmental summary of ancient lake occupation, burials, food resources and dated footprints; individual dates have sampling uncertainties.

m10-australia-mungo.title: National Museum of Australia, Mungo Lady
m10-australia-mungo.notes: Museum synthesis on burial, chronology, and repatriation including Indigenous historical context; reports selected scholarship rather than presenting a full excavation monograph.

m10-australia-budj.title: Budj Bim Cultural Landscape — UNESCO World Heritage Centre
m10-australia-budj.notes: Recognition of Gunditjmara wetland engineering across millennia; no implication that every component dates to the beginning of the sequence.

m10-australia-gunditjmara.title: Gunditjmara Culture and Country — Budj Bim Cultural Landscape
m10-australia-gunditjmara.notes: Local cultural landscape and community history, including living knowledge; community source speaks to Gunditjmara Country, not a general Australian cultural model.

m10-australia-martu.title: R. Bliege Bird et al., The fire stick farming hypothesis (PNAS, 2008)
m10-australia-martu.notes: Research combines observations of Martu burning/hunting with satellite analysis. Measured patterns are site-specific and recent, not direct millennia-long continuity evidence.

m10-andes-ayllu.title: Beth K. Scaffidi, Landscapes of Pre-Hispanic Andean Kinship: Ancestors, Ayllus and Relationality (2026)
m10-andes-ayllu.notes: Open-access review of ayllu and relational kinship and limits of archaeological genetic inference. Colonial ethnography should not be projected unchanged into earlier periods.

m10-andes-paracas.title: Economic Directness in the Western Andes: Paracas in the First Millennium BC (Latin American Antiquity, 2023)
m10-andes-paracas.notes: Excavated Paracas settlement and material evidence from the northern Nasca drainage; economic-directness model is place- and period-specific.

m10-andes-nmai.title: Smithsonian National Museum of the American Indian, The Great Inka Road: Building the Road
m10-andes-nmai.notes: Museum interpretation of mit’a, ayni, and road labor. Does not document every local form of reciprocity or every individual worker.

m10-andes-mitmaq.title: Di Hu et al., Food and Labour under Imperial Rule: mitmaqkuna (2024)
m10-andes-mitmaq.notes: Site-level archaeobotanical and labor-context research on Inka transplanted workers; cannot generalize a single enclave to all imperial populations.
