b11-juma04.title: Abdurahman Juma, Unguja Ukuu on Zanzibar: An Archaeological Study of Early Urbanism (2004)
b11-juma04.notes: Uppsala doctoral dissertation record: surface surveys, more than 200 cores, early occupation and trade. Abstract viewed; technical tables not independently reviewed.

b11-fitton17.title: Tom Fitton and Stephanie Wynne-Jones, Understanding the layout of early coastal settlement at Unguja Ukuu, Zanzibar (2017)
b11-fitton17.notes: Full accessible journal text on settlement mapping, magnetometry, waterfront and probable early mosque. Geophysical identification of worship space is interpretive.

b11-fitton22.title: Tom Fitton et al., Integrating spatial and legacy data to understand archaeological sites in their landscape: Unguja Ukuu (2022)
b11-fitton22.notes: Full open archaeological prospection article, including comparison of ground/remote sensing and 1990s records. Modern landscapes cannot stand for ancient shorelines.

b11-wynnejones21.title: Stephanie Wynne-Jones et al., Urban Chronology at a Human Scale on the Coast of East Africa (2021)
b11-wynnejones21.notes: Institutional research record and abstract confirm two less-than-forty-year house phases and episodic occupation; the site-wide implication is an interpretation.

b11-fauna17.title: Mary E. Prendergast et al., Dietary Diversity on the Swahili Coast: The Fauna from Two Zanzibar Trading Locales (2017)
b11-fauna17.notes: Peer-reviewed abstract on faunal assemblages at Fukuchani and Unguja Ukuu, fishing, introduced animals, contrasts in wild and domestic prey. Sampling is site-specific.

b11-tumbe13.title: Jeffrey Fleisher and Adria LaViolette, The early Swahili trade village of Tumbe, Pemba Island (2013)
b11-tumbe13.notes: Publisher abstract supports intensive exchange and possible shell-bead production in household settings without pronounced excavated stratification. Not proof of equality.

b11-pemba09.title: Adria LaViolette and Jeffrey Fleisher, The Urban History of a Rural Place: Pemba, 700–1500 (2009)
b11-pemba09.notes: Published article summary on Tumbe, Chwaka, and the pre-1500 political economy; accessible article excerpts discuss pearl millet, local domestic imports, and site-size uncertainty.

b11-pemba18.title: Jeffrey Fleisher and Adria LaViolette, Developments in Rural Life on the Eastern African Coast (2018)
b11-pemba18.notes: Publisher abstract on Kimimba and Tumbe, Kaliwa and Chwaka. Rural comparisons are not coast-wide statistics.

b11-pemba10.title: Jeffrey Fleisher, Swahili Synoecism: Rural Settlements and Town Formation on the Central East African Coast (2010)
b11-pemba10.notes: Journal abstract on northern Pemba regional survey, population movement, eleventh-century nucleation, new towns with coral mosques. Synoecism is interpretive.

b11-bead08.title: James L. Flexner, Jeffrey B. Fleisher and Adria LaViolette, Bead grinders and early Swahili household economy (2008)
b11-bead08.notes: AfricaBib scholarly abstract reports decentralized and nonstandardized grooved-tool manufacture; whether tools were used precisely for shell bead grinding remained debated.

b11-ett11.title: Jeffrey Fleisher and Stephanie Wynne-Jones, Ceramics and the Early Swahili: Deconstructing the Early Tana Tradition (2011)
b11-ett11.notes: Peer-reviewed article abstract and institutional metadata document east African shared pottery and varying regional forms. Ceramic similarity alone cannot establish shared ethnicity.

b11-ett13.title: Stephanie Wynne-Jones and Jeffrey Fleisher, Ceramics and Society: Early Tana Tradition and the Swahili Coast (2013)
b11-ett13.notes: Open data paper records 2000-plus sherds, forty variables, eight selected coastal and hinterland sites, and comparative sampling limits.

b11-ett23.title: Stephanie Wynne-Jones, Connecting the Dots: Ceramics and the Creation of Foundational Narratives in East African Archaeology (2023)
b11-ett23.notes: Open historical archaeology commentary on Phillipson 1979 survey at lower Tana and changing archaeological narratives. Does not imply all finds have same origins.

b11-shanga-horton.title: Mark C. Horton, Early Muslim Trading Settlements on the East African Coast: New Evidence from Shanga
b11-shanga-horton.notes: Excavation article excerpt on Shanga, early mosque interpretations and African settlement. Oldest phase interpretations disputed; the full monograph not reviewed.

b11-ray22.title: Daren E. Ray, Recycling Interdisciplinary Evidence: Abandoned Hypotheses and African Historiologies (2022)
b11-ray22.notes: Full open article covering Shungwaya debates, Helm settlement surveys, and named Mijikenda elder Thomas Govi. Later narratives and interpretive frameworks are not firsthand testimony from the eighth century.

b11-kaya-unesco.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Sacred Mijikenda Kaya Forests
b11-kaya-unesco.notes: UNESCO synopsis of sacred kayas and stewardship, mostly from sixteenth century onward. No direct eighth-century Shanga site chronology.

b11-kaya-ich.title: UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage, Traditions and practices associated with the Kayas
b11-kaya-ich.notes: Public heritage record on living Mijikenda practices and elders. A contemporary description, not a dated account of early medieval ritual.

b11-chibuene12.title: Paul Sinclair, Anneli Ekblom and Marilee Wood, Trade and society on the south-east African coast: Chibuene (2012)
b11-chibuene12.notes: Publisher abstract/extract documents Chibuene coastal imports and proposed inland links including Schroda. Full exchange paths remain reconstructed.

b11-chibuene-ekblom.title: Anneli Ekblom, Livelihood Security, Vulnerability and Resilience: Chibuene (2012)
b11-chibuene-ekblom.notes: PubMed abstract of archaeological-environmental and contemporary interview synthesis. Temporal continuity is argued, not established identically for all social institutions.

b11-letaba25.title: Alexander Antonites et al., New evidence for early Indian Ocean trade routes into the South African interior (2025)
b11-letaba25.notes: Open PNAS article reports fourteen glazed sherds at Le6, associated late-9th/10th century dating, and rival hypothesized routes. Cannot directly identify port of entry.

b11-moz-unesco.title: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Manyikeni and Chibuene — Mozambique Tentative List (1997)
b11-moz-unesco.notes: State-party tentative heritage nomination, NOT an inscribed World Heritage Site. Includes Chibuene imports and later Manyikeni remains, with differing site chronologies.

b12-loth18.notes: Open research article with excavation, grave distribution, ornament, site plans and radiocarbon table; estimates of whole cavity and social readings remain inferences.

b12-lothbio20.title: E. A. Sawchuk et al., The bioarchaeology of mid-Holocene pastoralist cemeteries west of Lake Turkana, Kenya (2020)
b12-lothbio20.notes: Publisher record and visible site figures/abstract used as cemetery comparison, not a complete independent mortality census.

b12-lothnews18.title: Turkana Basin Institute / Stony Brook University, Archaeologists reveal massive ancient cemetery (2018)
b12-lothnews18.notes: Institutional public explanation of researchers’ findings; not independent excavation evidence.

b12-lux18.title: Katherine M. Grillo et al., Pastoral Neolithic Settlement at Luxmanda, Tanzania (2018)
b12-lux18.notes: Excavation survey, occupation dates, ceramics and faunal analysis; bone assemblages sample surviving deposits, not entire diets.

b12-lux20.title: Katherine M. Grillo et al., Grinding-stone features from the Pastoral Neolithic at Luxmanda, Tanzania (Antiquity 2020)
b12-lux20.notes: Excavated concentrations of lower grinding stones and associated materials; alternative functions and settlement mobility are explicitly unresolved.

b12-lux26.title: Carolina Jiménez-Arteaga et al., Plant processing and foodways in the Pastoral Neolithic: Microbotanical evidence from grinding stones at Luxmanda, Tanzania (2026)
b12-lux26.notes: Accessible September 2026 publisher abstract/highlights, rather than full methods text: 44 residues from 33 stones and range of local plants; not evidence of domesticated cereal cultivation.

b12-luxdna17.title: Mary E. Prendergast et al., Reconstructing Prehistoric African Population Structure (2017)
b12-luxdna17.notes: Ancient DNA discussion includes Luxmanda individual, early dates and long-distance obsidian; an individual genome does not provide a population language or a whole-settlement census.

b12-kans24.title: Peter R. Schmidt et al., Remaking the Late Holocene Environment of Western Uganda: Archaeological Perspectives on Kansyore and Later Settlers (2024)
b12-kans24.notes: Multi-site Ndali Crater Lakes archaeological, environmental and linguistic reconstruction; interaction narratives and language associations are attributed interpretations.

b12-kans22.title: Mica B. Jones and Ruth Tibesasa, Kansyore fisher-hunter-gatherers abandoned the northeastern Lake Victoria shoreline during an arid period (2022)
b12-kans22.notes: Oxford publication abstract of Namundiri A radiocarbon/fauna reassessment, not full reconstruction of every Kansyore site.

b12-kakapel24.title: Steven T. Goldstein, Natalie G. Mueller et al., Early agriculture and crop transitions at Kakapel Rockshelter (Proc. Royal Society B 2024)
b12-kakapel24.notes: Open article and indexed full-text results on phases, directly dated cowpea, later finger millet/sorghum; single early pea is not directly dated and remains taxonomically ambiguous.

b12-kakapel25.title: Steven T. Goldstein et al., Cultural, economic, and settlement shifts over the last 9,000 years at Kakapel Rockshelter (PLOS ONE 2025)
b12-kakapel25.notes: Detailed occupation and regional survey study, with caveats about scale, associating subsistence shifts and population changes.

b12-crowther18.title: Alison Crowther et al., Subsistence mosaics, forager-farmer interactions, and the transition to food production in eastern Africa (2018)
b12-crowther18.notes: Regional synthesis; sections reviewed in indexed excerpts. Cannot override directly dated Kakapel plant remains.

b12-tsavo05.title: Chapurukha M. Kusimba, Sibel B. Kusimba and David K. Wright, The Development and Collapse of Precolonial Ethnic Mosaics in Tsavo, Kenya (2005)
b12-tsavo05.notes: Journal abstract supports region-wide mosaic of economies and ironworking; not treated as a fully inspected excavation report.

b12-tsavoms.title: Chapurukha M. Kusimba, Maritime Exchange Networks and Urban-Centered States in Ancient East Africa (research manuscript)
b12-tsavoms.notes: Author manuscript provides Tsavo iron furnace data and radiocarbon discussion. Hypotheses about ivory hunting and exchange remain hypotheses; terrace descriptions partly incorporate later oral testimony.

b12-tsavowright05.title: David K. Wright, New Perspectives on Early Regional Interaction Networks of East African Trade (2005)
b12-tsavowright05.notes: Record of investigations showing indirect contact without mandatory technology diffusion; not claimed to establish individual trade routes.

b12-kas17.title: Embedded histories and biogeographic interpretations of forest diversity at Mt. Kasigau, Kenya (2017)
b12-kas17.notes: Publisher extract and notes document local testimony and changing landscapes; modern interviews cannot establish exact ninth-century terrace tenure.

b12-engaruka17.title: Carol Lang and Daryl Stump, Geoarchaeological evidence for construction, irrigation, cultivation and resilience at Engaruka (2017)
b12-engaruka17.notes: Open publisher article with soil profiles, chemistry, field dates and explicit cautions against simple degradation/collapse stories.

b12-engaruka06.title: Daryl Stump, The Development and Expansion of the Field and Irrigation Systems at Engaruka, Tanzania (2006)
b12-engaruka06.notes: Abstract provides dating context, site extent and excavation chronology; full trench report not reviewed.

b12-engaruka10.title: Lars-Ove Westerberg, Karin Holmgren et al., The development of the ancient irrigation system at Engaruka: physical and societal factors (2010)
b12-engaruka10.notes: Abstract argues for correlations between chronology, regional climate, and caravan networks, not an independent definitive causal mechanism.

b13-mara26.notes: 2023-24 fieldwork and site report with explicit typological/dating limitations, including Nyabekwabi isolated sherd; regional pottery comparisons have variable chronology.

b13-ashley10.title: Ceri Z. Ashley, Towards a Socialised Archaeology of Ceramics in Great Lakes Africa (African Archaeological Review, 2010)
b13-ashley10.notes: Ceramic functions and changes across late first/early second millennia in Great Lakes Kenya/Uganda; inferences about authority are interpretive, not direct texts.

b13-lane07.title: Paul Lane et al., The transition to farming in eastern Africa: evidence from Wadh Lang'o and Usenge (Antiquity, 2007)
b13-lane07.notes: Publisher extract argues for long interactions, varied regional combinations and against simple universal replacement; full site tables not inspected.

b13-metal07.title: Paul T. Craddock et al., Early Iron Age iron-smelting debris from Rwanda and Burundi, East Africa (Historical Metallurgy 41[1], 2007; site posted 2021)
b13-metal07.notes: Journal abstract confirms slag phases and alternatives for clay-derived flux; the accessible summary does not specify every furnace or decision.

b13-vansina14.title: Jan Vansina, Linguistic Evidence for the Introduction of Ironworking into Bantu-Speaking Africa (History in Africa)
b13-vansina14.notes: Debates over early metallurgy origins and dates; archaeological charcoal cannot automatically settle linguistic chronology.

b13-schmidt97.title: Peter R. Schmidt, Archaeological Views on a History of Landscape Change in East Africa (Journal of African History, 1997)
b13-schmidt97.notes: Buhaya furnace and wood-species sequence, first-millennium woodland change, decline and later medieval renewed production; abstract only.

b13-schmidt78.title: Peter R. Schmidt and Donald H. Avery, Complex iron smelting and prehistoric culture in Tanzania (Science, 1978)
b13-schmidt78.notes: Authors report Haya preheating and steel-production reconstruction based on ethnographic, technical and archaeological study; do not generalize to every ancient furnace.

b13-kyazike22.title: Elizabeth Kyazike, Hunter-Gatherer/Farmer Interactions in Uganda (Oxford Research Encyclopedia of Anthropology, 2022)
b13-kyazike22.notes: Co-occurrence of Kansyore and Urewe cultural materials at Kansyore Island interpreted as contact/coexistence; no complete layer-by-layer proof reviewed.

b13-nature24.title: Cesar A. Fortes-Lima et al., The genetic legacy of the expansion of Bantu-speaking peoples in Africa (Nature 625, 2024)
b13-nature24.notes: Large living-participant dataset, 12 selected Late Iron Age genomes from southern/south-central Africa, modeled founder effect and genetic admixture; no DNA-to-language identity correspondence.

b13-yanovich25.title: Igor Yanovich, Reconstructing the Historical Structure of the Bantu Language Family (Annual Review of Linguistics 11, 2025)
b13-yanovich25.notes: Author argues against treating a particular linguistic phylogeny and archaeological/genetic alignment as certain; critical position, not consensus denial of language expansion.

b13-bostoen23.title: Koen Bostoen, Bantu Expansion (Encyclopedia of Ancient History: Asia and Africa, 2023)
b13-bostoen23.notes: Representative cross-disciplinary view of major language and population dispersal; details inaccessible beyond abstract.

b13-sutton93.title: J. E. G. Sutton, The Antecedents of the Interlacustrine Kingdoms (Journal of African History 34, 1993)
b13-sutton93.notes: Ntusi approx. eleventh-fifteenth-century settlement, later Bigo earthworks, cattle and grain; questions literal Cwezi royal identification.

b13-robertshaw01.title: Peter Robertshaw, The age and function of the ancient earthworks of western Uganda (Uganda Journal 47, 2001)
b13-robertshaw01.notes: 15th-16th-century chronology for Munsa/Kibengo trenches, Bigo maybe somewhat older; protection, crops, exchange and symbolic functions proposed, not settled.

b13-robertshaw02.title: Peter Robertshaw, The ancient earthworks of western Uganda: capital sites of a Cwezi empire? (Uganda Journal 48, 2002)
b13-robertshaw02.notes: Argues archaeology does not establish ancient singular Cwezi empire; proposes several contemporary polities, not conclusive proof.

b13-robertshaw97.title: Peter Robertshaw, Munsa Earthworks: A Preliminary Report on Recent Excavations (Azania 32, 1997)
b13-robertshaw97.notes: Munsa hill stratigraphy, iron working, probable grain storage, burial and beads; activity phases span much later than construction.

b14-janzen21.title: Anneke Janzen et al., Distinguishing African Bovids Using Zooarchaeology by Mass Spectrometry (PLOS ONE 16, 2021, e0251061)

b14-goldstein21.title: Steven T. Goldstein et al., Revisiting Kalundu Mound, Zambia (African Archaeological Review 38, 2021, 625–655)

b14-phillipson72.title: D. W. Phillipson, Early Iron Age Sites on the Zambian Copperbelt (Azania 7, 1972, 93–128)

b14-dlamini16.title: Nonhlanhla Dlamini, Alan Morris, and Judith Sealy, Carbon Isotopes and Dental Caries as Evidence for Regional Variation in the Diets of Early Farming Communities from Katanga (Journal of African Archaeology 14, 2016, 135–153)

b16-davis24.title: Dylan S. Davis, Robert J. DiNapoli, Gina Pakarati, Terry L. Hunt, and Carl P. Lipo, Island-wide characterization of agricultural production challenges the demographic collapse hypothesis for Rapa Nui, Science Advances 10 (2024)

b17-mixtec-codex.title: Claremont Colleges Library, Codex Zouche-Nuttall collection catalog (British Museum object summary)
b17-mixtec-codex.notes: Forty-seven painted deerskin leaves carry two narratives: lineage histories and the biography of Eight Deer Jaguar-Claw; catalog notes a Florence-to-Britain collecting history.

b17-mixtec-book.title: Robert Lloyd Williams, The Complete Codex Zouche-Nuttall: Mixtec Lineage Histories and Political Biographies, University of Texas Press (2013)
b17-mixtec-book.notes: Provides detailed sections for obverse lineages, reverse biography, Eight Deer’s relationships, chronology and reading conventions; full book not reviewed.

b17-mixtec-albany.title: University at Albany Libraries, Mesoamerican Codices: Nuttall (Mixtec), Special Collections guide
b17-mixtec-albany.notes: Describes obverse genealogical narratives and reverse Eight Deer biography; guide date conventions differ from some published reconstructions, so no specific birth year is inferred from guide alone.

b17-mixtec-colombino.title: Library of Congress World Digital Library, Codex Colombino (manuscript catalog and digitization)
b17-mixtec-colombino.notes: Describes a separately surviving Mixtec screenfold with Eight Deer and Four Wind histories, associated with the Becker I fragment; object catalog not an independent proof that all events occurred as portrayed.

b17-mixtec-joyce.title: Arthur A. Joyce, Andrew G. Workinger, Byron Hamann, Peter Kroefges, Maxine Oland and Stacie M. King, Lord 8 Deer “Jaguar Claw” and the Land of the Sky: The Archaeology and History of Tututepec, Latin American Antiquity 15 (2004), 273–297
b17-mixtec-joyce.notes: Surveys and excavations compare a politically powerful coastal center with pictorial foundation histories. Authorship confirmed from journal issue and university scholarly index.
b17-mixtec-joyce.locator: Abstract on foundation, scale, archaeology and codices

b17-pur-ceramics.title: Anna S. Cohen and colleagues, Local Production and Developing Core Regions: Ceramic Characterization in the Lake Pátzcuaro Basin, Western Mexico, Latin American Antiquity (2022)
b17-pur-ceramics.notes: Neutron activation analysis of pottery from four basin sites finds eight compositional groups, local recipes persisting through imperial formation and complex participation.
b17-pur-ceramics.locator: Abstract, historical background, ceramic NAA methods and discussion

b17-pur-landscape.title: Re-Envisioning Tarascan Temporalities and Landscapes, Journal of Archaeological Method and Theory (2017)
b17-pur-landscape.notes: Examines changing lake shorelines, visibility, settlement and the temptation to treat the contact-period Pátzcuaro landscape as timeless.
b17-pur-landscape.locator: Abstract, Pátzcuaro Basin ecology and settlement chronology

b17-pur-ecology.title: A Reexamination of Human-Induced Environmental Change within the Lake Pátzcuaro Basin, Michoacán, Mexico, PNAS (2003)
b17-pur-ecology.notes: Combines soils, lake fluctuations and settlement estimates; cautions against treating ancient intensification as inevitably environmentally destructive.
b17-pur-ecology.locator: Long-term landscape model, settlement phase and sedimentation record

b17-pur-inah.title: Instituto Nacional de Antropología e Historia, Zona Arqueológica de Tzintzuntzan
b17-pur-inah.notes: Identifies Tzintzuntzan as late Purépecha political/ceremonial center with yácatas, terraces and dynastic residences.
b17-pur-inah.locator: Relevancia cultural, monumental core and offices

b17-pur-metal.title: Instituto Nacional de Antropología e Historia, Espacio y tiempo en Tzintzuntzan
b17-pur-metal.notes: Discusses copper working, hammered and cast metals, workshops and supply from Tierra Caliente; broad museum interpretation rather than quantitative ore provenance study.
b17-pur-metal.locator: Museum description of metal technology and materials

b17-pur-relation.title: Angélica Jimena Afanador-Pujol, The Relación de Michoacán (1539–1541) and the Politics of Representation in Colonial Mexico, University of Texas Press (2015)
b17-pur-relation.notes: Analyzes friar, Indigenous elites and native artists who shaped a mid-sixteenth-century source; narratives and images reveal colonial power negotiations, not neutral eyewitness to earlier centuries.

b17-land-census.title: Barbara J. Williams and H. R. Harvey, Content, Provenience, and Significance of the Codex Vergara and the Códice de Santa María Asunción, American Antiquity 53 (1988)
b17-land-census.notes: Records households and property in seventeen localities near Tepetlaoztoc, likely made around 1539–43; early colonial records cannot be used as direct census of 1490.
b17-land-census.locator: Abstract on 17 localities and recording date

b17-land-pnas.title: María del Carmen Jorge, Barbara J. Williams, C. E. Garza-Hume and Arturo Olvera, Mathematical Accuracy of Aztec Land Surveys Assessed from Records in the Codex Vergara, PNAS 108 (2011)
b17-land-pnas.notes: Compares depicted field areas, dimensions and geometrical estimates; three quarters of reported areas within 5 percent of theoretical maxima under specified modeling assumptions.
b17-land-pnas.locator: Abstract, area calculation, comparisons and methods

b17-land-harvey.title: Herbert R. Harvey, Household and Family Structure in Early Colonial Tepetlaoztoc: An Analysis of the Códice de Santa María Asunción, Estudios de Cultura Náhuatl (1986)
b17-land-harvey.notes: Identifies household-census, parcel measurement and computed area registers in Santa María Asunción and Vergara.

b17-land-loc.title: Library of Congress World Digital Library, Codex Vergara (digitized manuscript catalog)
b17-land-loc.notes: Collection record describes households, names, villages, parcels and taxation context; its claim of Spanish authorship is not adopted over manuscript specialists.
b17-land-loc.locator: Collection summary, first folios, parcel description

b17-land-selden.title: Bodleian Libraries, Non-Destructive Analysis of Early Mesoamerican Manuscripts Conservation Project
b17-land-selden.notes: Preserves context of five pictorial manuscripts, including preconquest and colonial examples; survival sample is highly selective.
